     1	# Add Dispatch Sandbox Enforcement
     2	
     3	> Parent roadmap: `dispatch-governance` (item `dg-07`)
     4	> Change ID: `add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement`
     5	> Effort: M
     6	> Depends on: `dg-03` (isolation posture), `dg-06` (orchestrator obeys router)
     7	> Related: `symphony/trust-posture-binding` (priority 12) — declaration layer
     8	
     9	## Why
    10	
    11	The coordinator has an `isolation` field that means nothing.
    12	
    13	`agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py:264` declares
    14	`VALID_ISOLATION_MODES = {"worktree", "sandbox", "none"}`. The value is schema-validated,
    15	stored on `AgentEntry`, exposed through `get_agent_isolation()` (`agents_config.py:979`),
    16	and asserted in `tests/test_agents_config_isolation.py:170` — which pins `codex` to
    17	`"sandbox"`. **No production caller reads it.** An agent declared `isolation: sandbox`
    18	today runs exactly like one declared `isolation: none`.
    19	
    20	Three adjacent gaps compound it:
    21	
    22	**Worktree isolation is concurrency isolation, not security isolation.** The invariant in
    23	`docs/guides/worktree-management.md` is rigorously enforced — one agent, one worktree, one
    24	branch, guarded by `checkout_policy.py require-mutation`. It stops agents corrupting each
    25	other's git state. It does not stop a dispatched agent reading `~/.ssh/id_rsa` or POSTing
    26	the repository to a pastebin, because a worktree is an ordinary directory owned by the
    27	ordinary uid.
    28	
    29	**Network policy is advisory.** `network_policies.py` (90 lines) answers `check_domain()`
    30	through `policy_engine.py:361`. An agent must *voluntarily ask permission*. Nothing
    31	enforces the answer at the socket. This is the same defect `add-coordinator-llm-gateway`
    32	names for spend: *"that ceiling is advisory — enforced by post-hoc reconciliation, not at
    33	request time."* Same shape, different resource.
    34	
    35	**Sandbox intent is already expressed, in three incompatible dialects, enforced by nobody.**
    36	`agents.yaml:60-66` and `:131-137`:
    37	
    38	```yaml
    39	review:      { args: ["--print", "--allowedTools", "Read,Grep,Glob"] }   # claude
    40	review:      { args: ["exec", "-s", "read-only"] }                        # codex
    41	alternative: { args: ["exec", "-s", "workspace-write"] }
    42	```
    43	
    44	The file's own header comment says "the dispatch mode controls sandbox permissions." That
    45	is a policy statement per dispatch mode, written three different ways, enforced by whatever
    46	each vendor felt like implementing, verifiable by us in no way at all.
    47	
    48	Meanwhile `symphony/trust-posture-binding` commits to a posture artifact declaring
    49	"sandbox mode, network allowlist" bound to `policy_engine.py` so posture is
    50	"**enforceable, not just documented**." There is currently no mechanism that could make
    51	it enforceable. This change is that mechanism.
    52	
    53	### Why now, and why at dispatch
    54	
    55	Dispatched vendor CLIs are the sharpest edge in the system: `review_dispatcher.py`
    56	spawns `claude`, `codex`, `gemini` and friends with prompts assembled from repository
    57	content, and every one of them inherits the full ambient authority of the developer's
    58	uid — SSH keys, cloud credentials, shell rc files, unrestricted egress. That is code we
    59	did not write, driven by prompts we do not fully review.
    60	
    61	It is also, conveniently, a single chokepoint. `CliVendorAdapter.build_command()`
    62	(`review_dispatcher.py:218`) constructs `cmd`; `subprocess.run(cmd, ...)` at `:279` and
    63	`:521` executes it. One injection site covers every vendor.
    64	
    65	The pressure is increasing, not static. `TRUST_POSTURE.md` exists precisely to let
    66	operators flip human gates from `block` to `auto`. Every gate flipped removes a human
    67	from the loop. Machine-level containment is what should backfill the removed human, and
    68	right now nothing does.
    69	
    70	## What Changes
    71	
    72	### New: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py`
    73	
    74	A pure, side-effect-free renderer. Takes a resolved isolation decision plus the
    75	coordinator's network policy and worktree root; returns a runtime-specific policy
    76	document plus an argv wrapper.
    77	
    78	- `resolve_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode, ...) -> IsolationDecision` — consults
    79	  the task router when reachable, falls back to `get_agent_isolation()` from
    80	  `agents.yaml`, then to `none`. Mirrors the precedence ladder already established in
    81	  `environment_profile.py`.
    82	- `render_srt_settings(decision, worktree_root, network_policy) -> dict` — emits srt's
    83	  JSON settings shape: `allowWrite` scoped to the worktree root, `denyRead` covering
    84	  credential paths, `network.allowedDomains` from the coordinator's policy.
    85	- `wrap_command(cmd, decision) -> list[str]` — returns `cmd` unchanged when isolation is
    86	  not `sandbox` or the runtime is unavailable; otherwise returns the wrapped argv.
    87	
    88	The renderer is deliberately runtime-shaped but not runtime-bound: `render_srt_settings`
    89	is one function beside a `render_*` seam, so an OpenShell YAML or container-args renderer
    90	is an addition rather than a rewrite. Both candidate runtimes are pre-1.0 (srt is a
    91	"research preview"; OpenShell is "alpha — single-player mode"), which makes the seam a
    92	requirement rather than speculative generality.
    93	
    94	### Modified: `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`
    95	
    96	`CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()` and `dispatch_async()` call `wrap_command()` between
    97	`build_command()` and `subprocess.run()`. No other logic moves.
    98	
    99	### Modified: `skills/shared/environment_profile.py`
   100	
   101	`isolation_provided: bool` widens to a two-dimensional posture — filesystem and network
   102	isolation reported separately — because a container gives strong filesystem isolation and
   103	wide-open egress, and this change must be able to say "skip the filesystem sandbox here,
   104	still enforce the network allowlist."
   105	
   106	The existing detection ladder also has a live bug: planning this change inside a cloud
   107	harness returned `isolation_provided=False source=default`, because the container exposes
   108	none of `/.dockerenv`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, or `CODESPACES`. `worktree.py setup`
   109	consequently attempted a real worktree and failed on the already-checked-out branch. The
   110	heuristic layer gains the missing signals.
   111	
   112	Existing `bool` callers keep working through a compatibility property; `worktree.py` and
   113	`merge_worktrees.py` read the filesystem dimension.
   114	
   115	### Modified: `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`
   116	
   117	`get_agent_isolation()` gains a companion that resolves *effective* isolation for an
   118	`(agent_type, dispatch_mode)` pair, so `review` and `alternative` can carry different
   119	postures under one agent entry — which `agents.yaml` already implies and cannot express.
   120	
   121	### Modified: `agent-coordinator/src/network_policies.py`
   122	
   123	An export path that serializes the active policy into the shape `sandbox_profile.py`
   124	consumes. The policy stays authored in one place; enforcement becomes a rendering of it.
   125	
   126	### Degradation
   127	
   128	srt requires macOS (Seatbelt) or Linux (bubblewrap + socat + ripgrep). When the runtime
   129	is absent or the platform is unsupported, dispatch **proceeds unsandboxed**, emits a
   130	warning, and writes a coordinator audit event. This follows the degradation pattern
   131	already used in `vendor_health.py`. Fail-closed would break every developer on an
   132	unsupported platform for a control that is, by its authors' own account, a defense
   133	against confused agents rather than determined ones.
   134	
   135	## Non-Goals
   136	
   137	- **Sandbox lifecycle management in the coordinator.** No `sandbox_create` / `sandbox_destroy`
   138	  / connection brokering. That is OpenShell's entire product (a Rust gateway plus k3s); if
   139	  containerized isolation is needed later, dispatch should target OpenShell's API rather
   140	  than reimplementing a control plane. Related: `docker_manager.py` handles ParadeDB and
   141	  Colima lifecycle and must not grow into an agent sandbox manager — different problem,
   142	  different failure modes.
   143	- **Wrapping Bash inside skill scripts.** Many call sites, much broader blast radius,
   144	  deferred by explicit scope decision.
   145	- **Declaring the posture artifact.** `symphony/trust-posture-binding` owns declaration.
   146	  This change owns enforcement and consumes whatever that item declares.
   147	- **Protection against a determined exfiltrator.** See Trade-offs.
   148	
   149	## Approaches Considered
   150	
   151	### Approach 1 — OS-level wrapper at the dispatch chokepoint (**Recommended**)
   152	
   153	Render coordinator policy into an srt settings document and wrap the vendor argv in
   154	`CliVendorAdapter`.
   155	
   156	**Pros**
   157	- One injection site (`review_dispatcher.py:218` → `:279`) covers every current and
   158	  future vendor CLI, including vendors that ship no sandbox of their own.
   159	- Gives the existing advisory `network_policies.py` real teeth at the socket without
   160	  rewriting the policy model or moving where policy is authored.
   161	- Finally gives `isolation: sandbox` — already declared, validated, and tested — a
   162	  meaning, closing a gap the schema has advertised for some time.
   163	- srt is a single npm dependency with no daemon, no control plane, and no ops burden;
   164	  it is what Claude Code's own `/sandbox` uses.
   165	- Vendor-neutral: the same posture applies to `codex`, `gemini`, and any adapter added
   166	  later, rather than depending on each vendor's flags.
   167	
   168	**Cons**
   169	- Adds a Node dependency to a Python dispatch path.
   170	- Unsupported on Windows outside WSL2 (srt's Windows support is alpha).
   171	- OS-level sandboxing falls to a kernel bug; containers would be stronger.
   172	- srt is a research preview with an unstable interface.
   173	
   174	**Effort**: M
   175	
   176	### Approach 2 — Normalize vendor-native sandbox flags only
   177	
   178	Define a portable mode vocabulary (`read-only`, `workspace-write`) and map it onto each
   179	vendor's own flags, extending what `agents.yaml` already does.
   180	
   181	**Pros**
   182	- No new dependency; works on every platform the vendor CLIs work on.
   183	- Smallest diff by a wide margin; effort S.
   184	- Zero risk of breaking dispatch on unsupported platforms.
   185	
   186	**Cons**
   187	- Enforces nothing we control — we are trusting each vendor's implementation, with no way
   188	  to verify it and no recourse when it is weak or absent.
   189	- Vendors without a sandbox mode get no protection at all.
   190	- Does not cover `SdkVendorAdapter`, which makes direct API calls with no CLI to flag.
   191	- Leaves `isolation: sandbox` still meaningless, and leaves `network_policies.py` still
   192	  advisory — neither of the two gaps that motivate this change actually closes.
   193	
   194	**Effort**: S
   195	
   196	### Approach 3 — Coordinator-managed container sandboxes (OpenShell or bespoke)
   197	
   198	Give the coordinator sandbox lifecycle primitives; run dispatched agents inside containers
   199	with policy-enforced egress and injected credential providers.
   200	
   201	**Pros**
   202	- Strongest isolation boundary of the three; survives a kernel bug that defeats Seatbelt
   203	  or bubblewrap.
   204	- Credentials never touch the sandbox filesystem (OpenShell's provider model).
   205	- Handles the multi-tenant case this repo may eventually reach.
   206	
   207	**Cons**
   208	- Rebuilds, or takes a hard dependency on, an alpha "single-player mode" control plane.
   209	- Per-dispatch container startup latency against a review path that is currently a
   210	  subprocess spawn.
   211	- Substantial ops burden: image builds, registry, gateway lifecycle, k3s.
   212	- Overwhelmingly disproportionate to the threat model — the realistic failure is a
   213	  prompt-injected agent reading credentials, not a container escape.
   214	
   215	**Effort**: XL
   216	
   217	### Recommendation
   218	
   219	**Approach 1.** Approach 2 is cheaper but closes neither motivating gap: `isolation: sandbox`
   220	stays inert and network policy stays advisory, so it buys a vocabulary rather than a
   221	control. Approach 3 buys a stronger boundary than the threat model needs, at the cost of
   222	depending on an alpha control plane and adding container latency to every review dispatch.
   223	
   224	Approach 1 sits where the leverage is: one chokepoint, one dependency, enforcement of a
   225	policy model that already exists. It also leaves Approach 3 open — `render_srt_settings`
   226	sits behind a seam, so adopting OpenShell later means adding a renderer, not redoing the
   227	integration.
   228	
   229	## Trade-offs
   230	
   231	**Accepted: containment of confused agents over containment of determined ones.** srt's own
   232	documentation is explicit that an allowlist containing `github.com` is an exfiltration
   233	channel, that domain fronting works, and that an exposed Docker socket is a full escape.
   234	This repository's workflow *requires* `github.com`. What this change buys is protection
   235	against accidental credential reads and unplanned egress. It is not a containment boundary
   236	against an adversary who knows GitHub is reachable, and the specs must not claim otherwise.
   237	
   238	**Accepted: a Node dependency in a Python path** over building OS-sandboxing bindings
   239	ourselves.
   240	
   241	**Accepted: fail-open** over a hard guarantee, so unsupported platforms degrade instead of
   242	breaking. The audit event is what makes the degradation visible rather than silent.
   243	
   244	## Impact
   245	
   246	- **Specs**: `agent-coordinator` (isolation resolution, policy export), `skill-workflow`
   247	  (dispatch wrapping), `worktree` (posture dimensions)
   248	- **Code**: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` (new), `skills/shared/environment_profile.py`,
   249	  `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`,
   250	  `agent-coordinator/src/agents_config.py`, `agent-coordinator/src/network_policies.py`
   251	- **Config**: `agents.yaml` per-mode isolation
   252	- **Docs**: `docs/guides/worktree-management.md` (posture, not bool)
   253	
   254	### Coordination with in-flight changes
   255	
   256	- **`implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model`** — `POST /route/task` returns
   257	  `isolation` among its outputs. That change is the **producer** of the decision; this one
   258	  is the **consumer**. `resolve_isolation()` calls the router when reachable. Because the
   259	  router change already specifies "a local static fallback table when the coordinator is
   260	  down," this change is interface-bound to the router without being schedule-blocked by it:
   261	  the fallback is `get_agent_isolation()`, which exists today. The contract between them
   262	  must be pinned before either merges.
   263	- **`build-structured-vendor-result-channel`** — rewrites the same `CliVendorAdapter`
   264	  methods this change modifies. Direct merge-conflict risk; the two must not run
   265	  concurrently against `review_dispatcher.py`. Sequencing to be recorded in `design.md`.
   266	- **`add-coordinator-llm-gateway`** — same advisory-to-enforced argument applied to spend.
   267	  This change should follow its established shape rather than invent a parallel one.
   268	- **`symphony/trust-posture-binding`** — declaration layer. This change supplies the
   269	  enforcement its acceptance criterion ("enforceable, not just documented") requires.
     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Isolation SHALL be enforced at the dispatch chokepoint
     4	
     5	Every dispatched vendor CLI invocation SHALL pass through a single argv-wrapping seam between command construction and process execution, so that one injection site covers every vendor adapter.
     6	
     7	`CliVendorAdapter.build_command()` constructs the argv and `subprocess.run()` executes it. Wrapping between those two points is what makes the control total; wrapping inside individual adapters would leave each new vendor unprotected by default.
     8	
     9	#### Scenario: Every vendor passes through the same seam
    10	
    11	WHEN any vendor CLI is dispatched, synchronously or asynchronously
    12	THEN the constructed argv SHALL be passed through the wrapping seam before execution
    13	AND no adapter SHALL execute an argv that bypassed the seam.
    14	
    15	#### Scenario: Non-sandbox postures pass the argv through unchanged
    16	
    17	WHEN the resolved isolation decision is not `sandbox`
    18	THEN the seam SHALL return the argv unchanged
    19	AND dispatch behavior SHALL be identical to dispatch before this change.
    20	
    21	### Requirement: The sandbox profile renderer SHALL be pure and runtime-seamed
    22	
    23	The sandbox profile renderer SHALL be free of side effects, taking a resolved isolation decision together with the coordinator's network policy and the worktree root, and returning a runtime-specific policy document plus an argv wrapper.
    24	
    25	Both candidate runtimes are pre-1.0, so the renderer SHALL expose a per-runtime rendering seam such that supporting an additional runtime is an addition rather than a rewrite.
    26	
    27	#### Scenario: Rendering performs no side effects
    28	
    29	WHEN the renderer is invoked
    30	THEN it SHALL NOT mutate the filesystem, spawn a process, or contact the network
    31	AND the same inputs SHALL produce the same policy document.
    32	
    33	#### Scenario: Write scope is confined to the worktree root
    34	
    35	WHEN a policy document is rendered for a `sandbox` decision
    36	THEN write access SHALL be scoped to the supplied worktree root
    37	AND read access SHALL be denied for credential paths
    38	AND permitted network destinations SHALL be taken from the coordinator's network policy.
    39	
    40	#### Scenario: A second runtime is added without rewriting the renderer
    41	
    42	WHEN support for an additional sandbox runtime is introduced
    43	THEN it SHALL be added as an additional rendering function at the existing seam
    44	AND the resolution and wrapping logic SHALL remain unchanged.
    45	
    46	### Requirement: The authored network policy SHALL remain the single source of enforced destinations
    47	
    48	The coordinator's network policy SHALL remain authored in one place, and enforcement SHALL be a rendering of that policy rather than a second, independently-maintained allowlist.
    49	
    50	#### Scenario: Enforced destinations derive from the authored policy
    51	
    52	WHEN a sandbox policy document is rendered
    53	THEN its permitted network destinations SHALL be derived from the active coordinator network policy
    54	AND no destination SHALL be introduced that the authored policy does not permit.
    55	
    56	### Requirement: Unsupported platforms SHALL degrade openly rather than fail closed
    57	
    58	When the sandbox runtime is absent or the host platform is unsupported, dispatch SHALL proceed unsandboxed, SHALL emit a warning, and SHALL write a coordinator audit event recording that isolation was requested but not applied.
    59	
    60	Failing closed would break every developer on an unsupported platform for a control that is, by its authors' own account, a defense against confused agents rather than determined ones. Degrading silently would be worse: an operator would believe a containment control was active when it was not.
    61	
    62	#### Scenario: Missing runtime degrades with a warning and an audit event
    63	
    64	WHEN the resolved isolation decision is `sandbox`
    65	AND the sandbox runtime is not installed or the platform is unsupported
    66	THEN dispatch SHALL proceed without the sandbox
    67	AND a warning SHALL be emitted
    68	AND a coordinator audit event SHALL record that `sandbox` was requested and not applied.
    69	
    70	#### Scenario: Degradation is never silent
    71	
    72	WHEN dispatch proceeds unsandboxed after a `sandbox` decision
    73	THEN the outcome SHALL be observable from the audit trail alone
    74	AND the dispatch SHALL NOT report itself as sandboxed.

A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nA watchdog `ConfiguredCatalogSync` job materializes configured non-OpenRouter lane\nmodels in `model_catalog`. `agents.yaml` explicitly sets `catalog_vendor` and\n`endpoint_kind` for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus\n`vendor-cli`; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus `vendor-sdk`. CLI model\nIDs come from the canonical provider model map; SDK model IDs come only from the lane's\nSDK model/fallback list. The job inserts only missing identity rows, with enabled catalog\navailability and unknown price/posterior, and never overwrites existing pricing,\nposterior, availability, or refresh data. Registry probe/rate-limit state remains the live\nlane-availability source.\n\nOpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a\nmulti-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row\nbefore the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key. Missing or ambiguous\nidentity metadata is an explicit configuration miss, never filled from an agent-name\nsuffix or publisher guess. A real-agents.yaml test proves at least one configured CLI\nlane projects exactly after this bootstrap.\n\nThe routing path constructs a read-only `VendorRegistryService(audit=None)` because the\nrouter persists its own typed exclusions and atomic audit link; this avoids emitting one\ngeneric projection-miss audit row per request. The registry and catalog snapshots are\neach loaded once per request. A registry read or shape failure fails closed as\n`routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to catalog-only scoring. Catalog rows\nwith no exact configured lane projection are retained in `excluded` as\n`catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. DG-00's existing `unavailable` and\n`quota:exhausted` values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. openspec/changes/implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model/reviews/round-3/raw-pi-plan.txt:175:{"type":"message_start","message":{"role":"toolResult","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-e0689e421fe34f0d9d63ab45a11571a8","toolName":"read","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# Design: extend routing to vendor × location × isolation × dispatch mode\n\n## D1 — Extend one resolver and one public operation\n\nDG-04 extends the dg-00 `RoutingService.select_model()` pipeline, HTTP\n`POST /routing/select_model`, and MCP `select_model_for_task`. It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nA watchdog `ConfiguredCatalogSync` job materializes configured non-OpenRouter lane\nmodels in `model_catalog`. `agents.yaml` explicitly sets `catalog_vendor` and\n`endpoint_kind` for those lanes: local subscription CLIs use their exact vendor type plus\n`vendor-cli`; remote SDK lanes use their exact vendor type plus `vendor-sdk`. CLI model\nIDs come from the canonical provider model map; SDK model IDs come only from the lane's\nSDK model/fallback list. The job inserts only missing identity rows, with enabled catalog\navailability and unknown price/posterior, and never overwrites existing pricing,\nposterior, availability, or refresh data. Registry probe/rate-limit state remains the live\nlane-availability source.\n\nOpenRouter/local catalog rows remain owned by their existing refresh/probe jobs; for a\nmulti-publisher OpenRouter lane, exact model/endpoint/base-URL matching must yield one row\nbefore the row's catalog vendor becomes part of the four-field key. Missing or ambiguous\nidentity metadata is an explicit configuration miss, never filled from an agent-name\nsuffix or publisher guess. A real-agents.yaml test proves at least one configured CLI\nlane projects exactly after this bootstrap.\n\nThe routing path constructs a read-only `VendorRegistryService(audit=None)` because the\nrouter persists its own typed exclusions and atomic audit link; this avoids emitting one\ngeneric projection-miss audit row per request. The registry and catalog snapshots are\neach loaded once per request. A registry read or shape failure fails closed as\n`routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to catalog-only scoring. Catalog rows\nwith no exact configured lane projection are retained in `excluded` as\n`catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. DG-00's existing `unavailable` and\n`quota:exhausted` values remain accepted alongside DG-04's namespaced reasons. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. registered.\n\n#### Scenario: Legacy caller remains compatible\n\n- **WHEN** a caller sends only the dg-00 `task_signals.archetype` field\n- **THEN** the request SHALL remain valid\n- **AND** newly secret\nneed, parallelism, repository shape, roadmap policy, and optional location, isolation,\nand dispatch-mode constraints at the HTTP/MCP boundary.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid profile is rejected at MCP SHALL return the existing matching validation-error envelope.\n\n#### Scenario: Config rules consume typed signals\n\n- **WHEN** a validated `routing.yaml` rule matches a task-profile field\n- **THEN** its configured location, isolation, or dispatch-mode constraint SHALL be\n  applied deterministically\n- **AND** the matching rule ID SHALL be recorded in decision provenance.\n\n### Requirement: Registry-backed feasibility precedes utility\n\nThe router SHALL consume `VendorRegistryService` in process and remove infeasible\nlane/model assignments before invoking the existing dg-00 utility scorer. A periodic\nconfiguration-backed job SHALL materialize missing non-OpenRouter catalog identities from\nexplicit lane metadata and the canonical provider model map without overwriting live\ncatalog observations.\n\n#### Scenario: Configured lane identity is materialized\n\n- **WHEN** a configured non-OpenRouter lane model is absent from `model_catalog`\n- **THEN** the catalog job SHALL insert its explicit vendor, model, endpoint kind, and\n  base URL identity\n- **AND** SHALL NOT infer any field from agent-name or publisher-name heuristics\n- **AND** SHALL NOT overwrite existing price, posterior, availability, or refresh data.\n\n#### Scenario: Exact lane and catalog association\n\n- **WHEN** a registry lane projects a catalog model\n- **THEN** routing SHALL associate it only by the exact projected catalog vendor, model,\n  endpoint-kind, and base-URL identity\n- **AND** SHALL NOT infer association from agent ID suffixes, publisher names, or fuzzy\n  model strings.\n\n#### Scenario: Infeasible assignment cannot win\n\n- **WHEN** a lane is unavailable, rate limited, lacks the archetype or dispatch mode, or\n  violates location, isolation, or roadmap-policy constraints\n- **THEN** the lane/model assignment SHALL be excluded before dg-00 utility scoring\n- **AND** the exclusion SHALL carry a machine-readable reason.\n\n#### Scenario: Registry failure fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** the in-process registry snapshot cannot be loaded or validated\n- **THEN** routing SHALL fail with `routing-registry-unavailable`\n- **AND** SHALL NOT score catalog-only candidates or infer a lane association.\n\n#### Scenario: Unprojected catalog candidate remains explainable\n\n- **WHEN** a catalog row has no exact configured lane projection\n- **THEN** it SHALL NOT enter utility scoring\n- **AND** it SHALL appear in exclusions as `catalog:no-configured-lane`.\n\n#### Scenario: Feasible assignments retain dg-00 ranking\n\n- **WHEN** two or more lane/model assignments remain feasible\n- **THEN** their quality, cost, latency, headroom, and exploration ranking SHALL be\n  produced by the existing dg-00 scorer without a second utility function\n- **AND** equal scores SHALL be ordered by agent ID and exact catalog identity.\n\n### Requirement: Versioned deterministic routing policy\n\nRouting dimension rules SHALL be loaded from a schema-validated `routing.yaml` carrying\nan explicit schema version and policy version.\n\n#### Scenario: Policy edit changes a decision\n\n- **WHEN** a test changes a valid constraint rule or dispatch default in `routing.yaml`\n- **THEN** the resulting assignment SHALL change without a Python code edit\n- **AND** repeated evaluation of the same profile, registry snapshot, catalog snapshot,\n  and policy SHALL produce the same ordered candidates when exploration is disabled.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid policy fails loud\n\n- **WHEN** `routing.yaml` contains an unknown field, unsupported schema version, invalid\n  enum, duplicate rule ID, or reference to an unconfigured phase dispatch default\n- **THEN** policy loading SHALL fail before routing a task\n- **AND** SHALL NOT silently substitute permissive defaults.\n\n### Requirement: Additive assignment and provenance\n\nEvery selected candidate SHALL expose exact lane assignment fields and every persisted\ndecision SHALL retain the task profile, policy version/checksum, matched rules, excluded\nassignments, and source.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator decision is durable and auditable\n\n- **WHEN** the coordinator returns a routing decision\n- **THEN** the same decision ID and assignment SHALL be written to `routing_decisions`\n- **AND** a link-only coordinator audit event SHALL record decision ID, selected\n  agent/model, routing-policy version/checksum, source, and success\n- **AND** both records SHALL commit atomically before the response is returned.\n\n#### Scenario: Durable write cannot be established\n\n- **WHEN** the atomic decision-and-audit RPC fails\n- **THEN** neither record SHALL remain committed\n- **AND** HTTP SHALL return 503 detail `routing-durability-unavailable`\n- **AND** MCP SHALL return its existing matching 503 error envelope.\n\n#### Scenario: Persistence projection is bounded\n\n- **WHEN** permissive legacy task signals include undeclared values such as path lists\n- **THEN** the request remains valid for compatibility\n- **AND** persistence SHALL retain only declared task signals and the typed routing\n  profile, excluding all legacy extras.\n\n#### Scenario: Alternative candidates retain lane identity\n\n- **WHEN** feasible alternatives are returned\n- **THEN** each alternative SHALL retain its own exact `agent_id`, vendor type,\n  location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base URL.\n\n### Requirement: Honest local fallback\n\nA coordinator-unreachable client path SHALL derive a deterministic assignment only from\nthe checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, archetype model map, and caller's\nstatic model/provider inputs.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator is unreachable\n\n- **WHEN** the coordinator routing operation times out or is unreachable\n- **THEN** the local helper SHALL return the normal assignment shape with\n  `fallback=true`, `source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, and\n  `durable_audit=false`\n- **AND** SHALL NOT embed a roster, synthesize live availability, or claim a coordinator\n  audit record exists\n- **AND** its catalog key SHALL be null because no live catalog join occurred.\n\n#### Scenario: Existing static fallback equality is preserved\n\n- **WHEN** existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` adaptive routing is disabled, fails,\n  returns malformed data, or exceeds its bounded timeout\n- **THEN** the returned `ResolvedArchetype` SHALL equal the dg-00 static result exactly.\n"}]},"isError":false}

A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nThe registry and catalog snapshots are each loaded once per request. A registry read or\nshape failure fails closed as `routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to\ncatalog-only scoring. Catalog rows with no exact configured lane projection are retained\nin `excluded` as `catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or\nenforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nThe registry and catalog snapshots are each loaded once per request. A registry read or\nshape failure fails closed as `routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to\ncatalog-only scoring. Catalog rows with no exact configured lane projection are retained\nin `excluded` as `catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or\nenforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. It does not call routing before `dispatch_fn`,\nchange `phase_agent.py`, redispatch work, or add loop caps; DG-06 owns obedience.\nNo sandbox is launched; DG-07 owns enforcement.\n\n## D10 — Test-first packages and validation\n\nContract/config tests fail first, followed by pure policy/association tests, then service\nand transport/fallback tests. PostgreSQL coverage proves the additive JSONB decision\nround trip and durable audit link. Full coordinator and affected skills suites, Ruff,\nstrict mypy, strict OpenSpec, work-package DAG/scope checks, configured vendor-panel\nplan/implementation convergence, stacked PR CI, and exact static-fallback regression\nmust all pass before roadmap reconciliation.\n\nFramework-specific implementation follows the installed FastAPI/Pydantic versions and\ntheir official model/response documentation:\nhttps://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/models/ and\nhttps://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/response-model/.\n"}],"isError":false,"timestamp":1789600405271}}

It does not add\n`POST /route/task`, a second score function, or a second routing decision store.\nThe existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` meaning remains observable and\nunchanged; assignment and provenance are additive fields.\n\n## D2 — Preserve compatibility with an optional strict profile\n\nLegacy `task_signals` remains accepted with its current permissive extra-field\nbehavior because existing phase callers send fields such as `write_allow`. A new\noptional `routing_profile` is strict (`extra=forbid`) and types:\n\n- expected duration seconds;\n- scope category (`read-only|bounded-write|broad-write`);\n- interactivity (`interactive|headless`);\n- secret need category (`none|brokered|direct`), never a secret value;\n- positive parallelism;\n- repository shape (`single-package|monorepo|unknown`);\n- roadmap-policy constraints (allowed/excluded lane/vendor sets and an allowed-location set);\n- optional required location, isolation, and dispatch mode.\n\nPydantic validates the external boundary and FastAPI/MCP share the same request model.\nNew response objects are optional-with-default for legacy validation but are always\npopulated by a successful DG-04 service decision.\n\n## D3 — Rules are ordered, typed, and versioned\n\n`agent-coordinator/routing.yaml` carries `schema_version`, `policy_version`,\ndispatch-mode defaults, ordered first-match constraint rules, and a local-fallback\ndimension table. A dedicated loader validates unknown fields, duplicate IDs, enum values,\nranges, and phase dispatch defaults, then records a SHA-256 checksum of canonical file\nbytes.\n\nEach rule has a typed `when` predicate over the profile and a typed `constrain` block for\nlocation, isolation, and dispatch mode. Explicit request constraints take precedence;\notherwise the first matching rule that mentions a dimension constrains that dimension.\nThe phase-specific or global dispatch default is used only when no explicit or rule-based\ndispatch mode exists; unmatched location/isolation remain unconstrained. Rules narrow\nfeasibility and never add a second utility score. Changing a rule therefore changes the\nfeasible assignment set without code edits.\n\nThe Docker image copies the file beside `agents.yaml` and the loader resolves it from\n`ROUTING_CONFIG` or the package root, never the process working directory.\n\n## D4 — DG-01 is the only lane source and joins are exact\n\n`RoutingService` injects/loads `VendorRegistryService` in process and requests all\nlanes without `available_only` prefiltering so exclusion provenance is retained. For\neach lane it consumes dg-01's projected catalog models. It forms an assignment only when\nthe catalog candidate identity exactly equals the projection key:\n\n`(catalog_vendor, model, endpoint_kind, base_url)`.\n\n`base_url` and additive lane identity travel through `CandidateInput` and\n`ScoredCandidate`. Agent-name suffixes, provider/publisher guesses, substring matches,\nand fuzzy model names are forbidden. Missing or ambiguous projections remain explicit\nregistry misses and never become routable candidates.\n\nThe registry and catalog snapshots are each loaded once per request. A registry read or\nshape failure fails closed as `routing-registry-unavailable`; it never falls back to\ncatalog-only scoring. Catalog rows with no exact configured lane projection are retained\nin `excluded` as `catalog:no-configured-lane`, rather than disappearing silently.\n\n## D5 — Feasibility precedes DG-00 utility\n\nFor each exact lane/model pair, pure feasibility checks apply in deterministic order:\n\n1. live lane availability and lane/model rate limits;\n2. dispatchability, archetype, and requested/default dispatch mode;\n3. explicit/configured location and isolation constraints;\n4. roadmap-policy allow/exclude sets;\n5. catalog availability and dg-00 modality/quota constraints.\n\nReasons are machine-readable and sanitized. Only feasible lane/model candidates enter\nthe existing `score_and_rank`; DG-04 does not duplicate quality, posterior, cost,\nlatency, headroom, or exploration math. Multiple lanes may project the same catalog\nmodel, so the final stable order is `(-score, agent_id, catalog identity)`.\nLocation and isolation constraints use exact equality and dispatch mode uses exact\nmembership in the lane's configured modes; DG-04 does not infer an isolation-strength\nordering.\n\n## D6 — Assignment and provenance are additive\n\nA successful response adds top-level:\n\n- `assignment`: exact `agent_id`, `vendor_type`, `policy_vendor`,\n  `catalog_vendor`, location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base\n  URL;\n- `provenance`: source (`coordinator` or `local-static`), policy version/checksum,\n  matched rule IDs, rationale, persistence flag, durable-audit flag, and exact\n  lane/catalog key.\n\nThe selected candidate and every alternative carry their own additive `assignment`, while\nthe response retains the selected candidate's assignment/provenance at top level for\nconvenience. Existing selected-candidate fields remain intact for older consumers.\nExcluded assignments use a typed shape containing lane/catalog identity and a bounded\nmachine-readable reason.\n\n## D7 — Durable routing record is authoritative; audit event is linked\n\nThe existing `routing_decisions` row is the authoritative durable routing audit. Its\nsanitized `request` stores only declared task signals and the strict routing profile;\npermissive legacy extras such as `write_allow` are never persisted. Its `selected` object\nstores selected assignment plus provenance, and every item in `alternatives` stores its\nown assignment. `excluded` stores typed exclusion records. These are additive JSONB\nshapes and require no new table columns.\n\nMigration `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql` adds one transaction-scoped RPC that inserts the\n`routing_decisions` row and a sanitized link-only `routing_decision` audit-log event\natomically. The event contains only decision ID, selected agent/model, routing-policy\nversion/checksum, source, and success. The service awaits the RPC result and returns only\nafter both rows commit. RPC failure rolls back both writes and produces HTTP 503 detail\n`routing-durability-unavailable`; the MCP mirror returns its existing 503 error envelope.\nFire-and-forget `AuditService.log_operation()` is not used for this invariant, and neither\nan orphan decision nor an orphan audit link is observable. Existing dg-00 callers still\ntake their exact static fallback on any non-200 response.\n\nThe `routing_decisions.policy_version` column keeps dg-00 scorer version\n`linear-utility-v1`; the routing YAML version/checksum live in selected provenance. No raw\nsecret, environment value, prompt, free-form task-signal extra, or unbounded path list\nenters either record; only typed/bounded categories and rationale enter persistence.\n\n## D8 — Local fallback is configuration-derived and honest\n\nA skills-side bridge/helper may fall back only after transport timeout/unreachability. It\nloads the checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, and archetype model map,\nthen combines the caller's already-resolved static provider/model with the fallback\ndimension order. It never embeds a roster, fabricates availability, or performs fuzzy\nassociation.\n\nThe response has the normal assignment shape plus `fallback=true`,\n`source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, `durable_audit=false`, and a bounded\nfailure reason. Its catalog key is null because no live catalog join occurred. A local\nUUID is explicitly not retrievable from coordinator decision storage. Missing or invalid\nconfiguration fails loud; the helper does not invent permissive defaults.\n\nThe fallback table's order is only a deterministic choice among the lane's exact\nconfigured values while the coordinator is unreachable. It is not an isolation-strength\nprecedence or enforcement policy. The reusable helper lives in\n`skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/routing_fallback.py`, resolves repository config from\nan explicit root or discovered checkout root, and is used by bridge and HTTP-proxy\ndegradation paths.\n\nThe existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` fallback is not rewritten: disabled,\nfailure, malformed-response, and timeout paths still return the exact dg-00 static\n`ResolvedArchetype` object with no added reasons or fields.\n\n## D9 — DG-05/DG-06 boundaries remain closed\n\nDG-04 carries the lane's current configured isolation as data and may filter an explicit\nrequest. It does not define per-mode overrides, the isolation precedence ladder, or\nenforcement; DG-05 owns that contract. It does not call routing before `dispatch_fn`,\nchange `phase_agent.py`, redispatch work, or add loop caps; DG-06 owns obedience.\nNo sandbox is launched; DG-07 owns enforcement.\n\n## D10 — Test-first packages and validation\n\nContract/config tests fail first, followed by pure policy/association tests, then service\nand transport/fallback tests. openspec/changes/implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model/reviews/round-2/raw-pi-plan.txt:180:{"type":"tool_execution_end","toolCallId":"chatcmpl-tool-3879b1750f394be0bd59a26b64d00619","toolName":"read","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"## ADDED Requirements\n\n### Requirement: One additive routing surface\n\nThe coordinator SHALL extend `POST /routing/select_model` and its\n`select_model_for_task` MCP mirror with task-profile and assignment fields, and SHALL NOT\nadd a second task-routing endpoint or scoring path.\n\n#### Scenario: Existing HTTP and MCP surfaces stay aligned\n\n- **WHEN** the same valid task-routing request is submitted through HTTP and direct MCP\n- **THEN** both surfaces SHALL validate the same typed profile and return the same\n  assignment/provenance shape\n- **AND** no `POST /route/task` route SHALL be registered.\n\n#### Scenario: Legacy caller remains compatible\n\n- **WHEN** a caller sends only the dg-00 `task_signals.archetype` field\n- **THEN** the request SHALL remain valid\n- **AND** newly added input and output fields SHALL use additive defaults.\n\n### Requirement: Typed task-routing profile\n\nThe request SHALL type phase/archetype, expected duration, scope, interactivity, secret\nneed, parallelism, repository shape, roadmap policy, and optional location, isolation,\nand dispatch-mode constraints at the HTTP/MCP boundary.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid profile is rejected at the boundary\n\n- **WHEN** a task profile contains an invalid enum, negative duration, non-positive\n  parallelism, or malformed policy constraint\n- **THEN** HTTP SHALL return 422\n- **AND** direct MCP SHALL return the existing matching validation-error envelope.\n\n#### Scenario: Config rules consume typed signals\n\n- **WHEN** a validated `routing.yaml` rule matches a task-profile field\n- **THEN** its configured location, isolation, or dispatch-mode constraint SHALL be\n  applied deterministically\n- **AND** the matching rule ID SHALL be recorded in decision provenance.\n\n### Requirement: Registry-backed feasibility precedes utility\n\nThe router SHALL consume `VendorRegistryService` in process and remove infeasible\nlane/model assignments before invoking the existing dg-00 utility scorer.\n\n#### Scenario: Exact lane and catalog association\n\n- **WHEN** a registry lane projects a catalog model\n- **THEN** routing SHALL associate it only by the exact projected catalog vendor, model,\n  endpoint-kind, and base-URL identity\n- **AND** SHALL NOT infer association from agent ID suffixes, publisher names, or fuzzy\n  model strings.\n\n#### Scenario: Infeasible assignment cannot win\n\n- **WHEN** a lane is unavailable, rate limited, lacks the archetype or dispatch mode, or\n  violates location, isolation, or roadmap-policy constraints\n- **THEN** the lane/model assignment SHALL be excluded before dg-00 utility scoring\n- **AND** the exclusion SHALL carry a machine-readable reason.\n\n#### Scenario: Registry failure fails closed\n\n- **WHEN** the in-process registry snapshot cannot be loaded or validated\n- **THEN** routing SHALL fail with `routing-registry-unavailable`\n- **AND** SHALL NOT score catalog-only candidates or infer a lane association.\n\n#### Scenario: Unprojected catalog candidate remains explainable\n\n- **WHEN** a catalog row has no exact configured lane projection\n- **THEN** it SHALL NOT enter utility scoring\n- **AND** it SHALL appear in exclusions as `catalog:no-configured-lane`.\n\n#### Scenario: Feasible assignments retain dg-00 ranking\n\n- **WHEN** two or more lane/model assignments remain feasible\n- **THEN** their quality, cost, latency, headroom, and exploration ranking SHALL be\n  produced by the existing dg-00 scorer without a second utility function\n- **AND** equal scores SHALL be ordered by agent ID and exact catalog identity.\n\n### Requirement: Versioned deterministic routing policy\n\nRouting dimension rules SHALL be loaded from a schema-validated `routing.yaml` carrying\nan explicit schema version and policy version.\n\n#### Scenario: Policy edit changes a decision\n\n- **WHEN** a test changes a valid constraint rule or dispatch default in `routing.yaml`\n- **THEN** the resulting assignment SHALL change without a Python code edit\n- **AND** repeated evaluation of the same profile, registry snapshot, catalog snapshot,\n  and policy SHALL produce the same ordered candidates when exploration is disabled.\n\n#### Scenario: Invalid policy fails loud\n\n- **WHEN** `routing.yaml` contains an unknown field, unsupported schema version, invalid\n  enum, duplicate rule ID, or reference to an unconfigured phase dispatch default\n- **THEN** policy loading SHALL fail before routing a task\n- **AND** SHALL NOT silently substitute permissive defaults.\n\n### Requirement: Additive assignment and provenance\n\nEvery selected candidate SHALL expose exact lane assignment fields and every persisted\ndecision SHALL retain the task profile, policy version/checksum, matched rules, excluded\nassignments, and source.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator decision is durable and auditable\n\n- **WHEN** the coordinator returns a routing decision\n- **THEN** the same decision ID and assignment SHALL be written to `routing_decisions`\n- **AND** a link-only coordinator audit event SHALL record decision ID, selected\n  agent/model, routing-policy version/checksum, source, and success\n- **AND** both records SHALL commit atomically before the response is returned.\n\n#### Scenario: Durable write cannot be established\n\n- **WHEN** the atomic decision-and-audit RPC fails\n- **THEN** neither record SHALL remain committed\n- **AND** HTTP SHALL return 503 detail `routing-durability-unavailable`\n- **AND** MCP SHALL return its existing matching 503 error envelope.\n\n#### Scenario: Persistence projection is bounded\n\n- **WHEN** permissive legacy task signals include undeclared values such as path lists\n- **THEN** the request remains valid for compatibility\n- **AND** persistence SHALL retain only declared task signals and the typed routing\n  profile, excluding all legacy extras.\n\n#### Scenario: Alternative candidates retain lane identity\n\n- **WHEN** feasible alternatives are returned\n- **THEN** each alternative SHALL retain its own exact `agent_id`, vendor type,\n  location, isolation, dispatch mode, model, endpoint kind, and base URL.\n\n### Requirement: Honest local fallback\n\nA coordinator-unreachable client path SHALL derive a deterministic assignment only from\nthe checkout's validated `routing.yaml`, `agents.yaml`, archetype model map, and caller's\nstatic model/provider inputs.\n\n#### Scenario: Coordinator is unreachable\n\n- **WHEN** the coordinator routing operation times out or is unreachable\n- **THEN** the local helper SHALL return the normal assignment shape with\n  `fallback=true`, `source=local-static`, `persisted=false`, and\n  `durable_audit=false`\n- **AND** SHALL NOT embed a roster, synthesize live availability, or claim a coordinator\n  audit record exists\n- **AND** its catalog key SHALL be null because no live catalog join occurred.\n\n#### Scenario: Existing static fallback equality is preserved\n\n- **WHEN** existing `resolve_archetype_for_phase` adaptive routing is disabled, fails,\n  returns malformed data, or exceeds its bounded timeout\n- **THEN** the returned `ResolvedArchetype` SHALL equal the dg-00 static result exactly.\n"}]},"isError":false}

FILE:openspec/changes/implement-the-task-router-vendor-x-location-x-model/contracts/README.md
     1	# DG-04 routing contract overlay
     2	
     3	These contracts extend, rather than replace, the dg-00 model-routing contract at
     4	`openspec/changes/add-adaptive-model-router/contracts/openapi/v1.yaml`.
     5	
     6	- `openapi/v1.1.yaml` pins the additive `routing_profile`, `assignment`, and
     7	  `provenance` fields on `POST /routing/select_model`.
     8	- `config/routing.schema.json` is the schema for the deployed, versioned
     9	  `agent-coordinator/routing.yaml`.
    10	- `events/routing-decision.schema.json` pins the sanitized, link-only coordinator audit
    11	  event.
    12	- `events/routing-decision-record.schema.json` pins the bounded authoritative
    13	  `routing_decisions` row and strips permissive legacy task-signal extras.
    14	
    15	The existing `selected.vendor/model/endpoint_kind` fields keep their dg-00 meaning.
    16	No `POST /route/task` operation exists.

    19	    domain: str
