     1	"""Audit trail service for Agent Coordinator.
     2	
     3	Provides immutable, async logging of all coordination operations.
     4	Audit entries are append-only — the database enforces immutability via triggers.
     5	"""
     6	
     7	import asyncio
     8	import logging
     9	import time
    10	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    11	from datetime import datetime
    12	from typing import Any
    13	
    14	from .config import get_config
    15	from .db import DatabaseClient, get_db
    16	
    17	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18	
    19	
    20	@dataclass
    21	class AuditEntry:
    22	    """Represents an audit log entry."""
    23	
    24	    id: str
    25	    agent_id: str
    26	    agent_type: str | None
    27	    operation: str
    28	    parameters: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    29	    result: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    30	    duration_ms: int | None = None
    31	    success: bool | None = None
    32	    error_message: str | None = None
    33	    created_at: datetime | None = None
    34	    delegated_from: str | None = None
    35	
    36	    @classmethod
    37	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "AuditEntry":
    38	        created_at = None
    39	        if data.get("created_at"):
    40	            created_at = datetime.fromisoformat(
    41	                str(data["created_at"]).replace("Z", "+00:00")
    42	            )
    43	        return cls(
    44	            id=str(data["id"]),
    45	            agent_id=data["agent_id"],
    46	            agent_type=data.get("agent_type"),
    47	            operation=data["operation"],
    48	            parameters=data.get("parameters") or {},
    49	            result=data.get("result") or {},
    50	            duration_ms=data.get("duration_ms"),
    51	            success=data.get("success"),
    52	            error_message=data.get("error_message"),
    53	            created_at=created_at,
    54	            delegated_from=data.get("delegated_from"),
    55	        )
    56	
    57	
    58	@dataclass
    59	class AuditResult:
    60	    """Result of an audit logging operation."""
    61	
    62	    success: bool
    63	    entry_id: str | None = None
    64	    error: str | None = None
    65	
    66	    @classmethod
    67	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "AuditResult":
    68	        return cls(
    69	            success=data.get("success", False),
    70	            entry_id=data.get("entry_id") or data.get("id"),
    71	            error=data.get("error"),
    72	        )
    73	
    74	
    75	class AuditService:
    76	    """Service for audit trail logging and querying."""
    77	
    78	    def __init__(self, db: DatabaseClient | None = None):
    79	        self._db = db
    80	        #: Strong references to in-flight fire-and-forget insert tasks.
    81	        #:
    82	        #: ``asyncio`` keeps only a *weak* reference to a task, so a bare
    83	        #: ``create_task(...)`` whose result nobody holds may be garbage
    84	        #: collected before it runs. Holding the task until it completes is the
    85	        #: documented way to make fire-and-forget actually fire.
    86	        self._pending: set[asyncio.Task[AuditResult]] = set()
    87	
    88	    @property
    89	    def db(self) -> DatabaseClient:
    90	        if self._db is None:
    91	            self._db = get_db()
    92	        return self._db
    93	
    94	    async def log_operation(
    95	        self,
    96	        agent_id: str | None = None,
    97	        agent_type: str | None = None,
    98	        operation: str = "",
    99	        parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   100	        result: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   101	        duration_ms: int | None = None,
   102	        success: bool | None = None,
   103	        error_message: str | None = None,
   104	        delegated_from: str | None = None,
   105	        session_id: str | None = None,
   106	    ) -> AuditResult:
   107	        """Log a coordination operation to the audit trail.
   108	
   109	        When async_logging is enabled (default), this fires-and-forgets
   110	        the insert to avoid blocking the caller.
   111	
   112	        Also pushes the entry into the audit-triage ring buffer (D9)
   113	        for downstream LLM classification.  The push is synchronous
   114	        and microsecond-fast — no LLM involvement on the hot path.
   115	        """
   116	        config = get_config()
   117	        agent_id = agent_id or config.agent.agent_id
   118	        agent_type = agent_type or config.agent.agent_type
   119	
   120	        data = {
   121	            "agent_id": agent_id,
   122	            "agent_type": agent_type,
   123	            "operation": operation,
   124	            "parameters": parameters or {},
   125	            "result": result or {},
   126	            "duration_ms": duration_ms,
   127	            "success": success,
   128	            "error_message": error_message,
   129	            "delegated_from": delegated_from,
   130	        }
   131	
   132	        # Push to audit-triage ring buffer (D9: hot path, no LLM)
   133	        try:
   134	            from .audit_triage import get_triage_buffer
   135	
   136	            entry = AuditEntry(
   137	                id="",
   138	                agent_id=agent_id,
   139	                agent_type=agent_type,
   140	                operation=operation,
   141	                parameters=parameters or {},
   142	                result=result or {},
   143	                duration_ms=duration_ms,
   144	                success=success,
   145	                error_message=error_message,
   146	                delegated_from=delegated_from,
   147	            )
   148	            resolved_session_id = session_id or (config.agent.session_id or "unknown")
   149	            get_triage_buffer().push(entry, session_id=resolved_session_id)
   150	        except Exception:
   151	            # Never let triage buffer failures affect the audit hot path
   152	            pass
   153	
   154	        if config.audit.async_logging:
   155	            # Fire-and-forget: don't block the caller. `success=True` here means
   156	            # "accepted for writing", not "written" — the insert has not run yet.
   157	            task = asyncio.create_task(self._insert_audit_entry(data))
   158	            self._pending.add(task)
   159	            task.add_done_callback(self._pending.discard)
   160	            return AuditResult(success=True)
   161	        else:
   162	            return await self._insert_audit_entry(data)
   163	
   164	    async def drain(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
   165	        """Wait for in-flight fire-and-forget audit inserts to finish.
   166	
   167	        Callers that need the trail to exist before they continue — startup
   168	        projections, shutdown, and tests — await this. Without it a short-lived
   169	        process can exit before the loop ever runs the queued inserts, which is
   170	        indistinguishable from the writes failing.
   171	
   172	        Raises:
   173	            TimeoutError: if ``timeout`` elapses while inserts are still
   174	                outstanding. ``asyncio.wait`` returns a ``(done, pending)``
   175	                pair rather than raising on timeout, so a caller that ignores
   176	                it would see ``drain()`` return normally and believe the
   177	                audit trail is durable when it is not — the same
   178	                returned-but-unread failure mode ``_insert_audit_entry``
   179	                documents, one layer up. Raising makes the timeout
   180	                impossible to silently ignore.
   181	        """
   182	        if not self._pending:
   183	            return
   184	        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(set(self._pending), timeout=timeout)
   185	        if pending:
   186	            logger.error(
   187	                "Audit drain timed out after %.1fs with %d insert(s) still "
   188	                "outstanding — the audit trail is not guaranteed durable.",
   189	                timeout,
   190	                len(pending),
   191	            )
   192	            raise TimeoutError(
   193	                f"AuditService.drain() timed out after {timeout}s with "
   194	                f"{len(pending)} audit insert(s) still outstanding"
   195	            )
   196	
   197	    async def _insert_audit_entry(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> AuditResult:
   198	        """Insert an audit entry into the database.
   199	
   200	        Failures are logged rather than only returned. On the fire-and-forget
   201	        path nobody awaits the result, so a returned-but-unread error is the
   202	        same as no error at all — which is exactly how the audit trail came to
   203	        record nothing at all on the PostgreSQL backend for every operation:
   204	        ``log_operation`` built a payload containing ``delegated_from``, a
   205	        column ``audit_log`` did not have until migration 035, so every insert
   206	        raised, the exception was swallowed here, the failed result was
   207	        discarded by the caller, and callers were told ``success=True``.
   208	        """
   209	        try:
   210	            row = await self.db.insert("audit_log", data)
   211	            return AuditResult(success=True, entry_id=str(row.get("id", "")))
   212	        except Exception as e:
   213	            logger.error(
   214	                "Audit write failed for operation %r — the audit trail is "
   215	                "incomplete: %s",
   216	                data.get("operation"),
   217	                e,
   218	                exc_info=True,
   219	            )
   220	            return AuditResult(success=False, error=str(e))
   221	
   222	    async def query(
   223	        self,
   224	        agent_id: str | None = None,
   225	        operation: str | None = None,
   226	        since: datetime | None = None,
   227	        until: datetime | None = None,
   228	        limit: int = 50,
   229	        delegated_from: str | None = None,
   230	        change_id: str | None = None,
   231	    ) -> list[AuditEntry]:
   232	        """Query audit log entries with optional filters.
   233	
   234	        New filters (additive, backward-compatible; all optional):
   235	        - ``since``: ISO-8601 timestamp; returns entries with
   236	          ``created_at >= since``.
   237	        - ``change_id``: filters entries whose ``parameters`` JSONB column
   238	          contains ``{"change_id": "<id>"}`` (recorded by most call-sites)
   239	          OR whose ``agent_id`` maps to an ``agent_sessions.change_id``
   240	          match (fallback, best-effort).
   241	        """
   242	        query_parts = ["order=created_at.desc", f"limit={limit}"]
   243	
   244	        if agent_id:
   245	            query_parts.append(f"agent_id=eq.{agent_id}")
   246	        if operation:
   247	            query_parts.append(f"operation=eq.{operation}")
   248	        if since:
   249	            query_parts.append(f"created_at=gte.{since.isoformat()}")
   250	        if until:
   251	            query_parts.append(f"created_at=lte.{until.isoformat()}")
   252	        if delegated_from:
   253	            query_parts.append(f"delegated_from=eq.{delegated_from}")
   254	        if change_id:
   255	            # Filter on parameters JSONB containing change_id key.
   256	            # PostgREST/Supabase: parameters->>change_id=eq.<value>
   257	            # PostgresClient: appended as a raw query param string.
   258	            query_parts.append(f"parameters->>change_id=eq.{change_id}")
   259	
   260	        query = "&".join(query_parts)
   261	        rows = await self.db.query("audit_log", query)
   262	        return [AuditEntry.from_dict(row) for row in rows]
   263	
   264	    def timed(self, operation: str) -> "AuditTimer":
   265	        """Create a context manager for timing and logging an operation."""
   266	        return AuditTimer(self, operation)
   267	
   268	
   269	class AuditTimer:
   270	    """Context manager for timing operations and logging to audit trail."""
   271	
   272	    def __init__(self, service: AuditService, operation: str):
   273	        self.service = service
   274	        self.operation = operation
   275	        self._start: float = 0
   276	
   277	    async def __aenter__(self) -> "AuditTimer":
   278	        self._start = time.monotonic()
   279	        return self
   280	
   281	    async def __aexit__(
   282	        self,
   283	        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
   284	        exc_val: BaseException | None,
   285	        exc_tb: Any,
   286	    ) -> None:
   287	        duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - self._start) * 1000)
   288	        await self.service.log_operation(
   289	            operation=self.operation,
   290	            duration_ms=duration_ms,
   291	            success=exc_type is None,
   292	            error_message=str(exc_val) if exc_val else None,
   293	        )
   294	
   295	
   296	# Global service instance
   297	_audit_service: AuditService | None = None
   298	
   299	
   300	def get_audit_service() -> AuditService:
   301	    """Get the global audit service instance."""
   302	    global _audit_service
   303	    if _audit_service is None:
   304	        _audit_service = AuditService()
   305	    return _audit_service

     1	"""Canonical isolation vocabulary and precedence helpers."""
     2	
     3	from __future__ import annotations
     4	
     5	from collections.abc import Mapping
     6	from dataclasses import dataclass
     7	from typing import Literal, cast
     8	
     9	ISOLATION_MODES: tuple[str, ...] = ("none", "worktree", "sandbox")
    10	type IsolationMode = Literal["none", "worktree", "sandbox"]
    11	type IsolationSource = Literal["router", "agents_yaml", "default"]
    12	
    13	
    14	class IsolationContractError(ValueError):
    15	    """A supplied isolation value is not part of the pinned contract."""
    16	
    17	
    18	@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
    19	class IsolationResolution:
    20	    value: IsolationMode
    21	    source: IsolationSource
    22	
    23	
    24	def validate_isolation(value: object, *, rung: str) -> IsolationMode:
    25	    """Validate a present value and name its provenance on failure."""
    26	    if not isinstance(value, str) or value not in ISOLATION_MODES:
    27	        raise IsolationContractError(f"invalid isolation value at {rung}: {value!r}")
    28	    return cast(IsolationMode, value)
    29	
    30	
    31	def configured_isolation_value(
    32	    configured: Mapping[str, object], dispatch_mode: str | None
    33	) -> object | None:
    34	    """Return a present mode override, then the entry-level value.
    35	
    36	    Values are intentionally returned without truthiness coercion so callers
    37	    can distinguish absence from an invalid present value such as ``""``.
    38	    ``sandbox`` is a posture label here; enforcement remains a separate concern.
    39	    """
    40	    cli = configured.get("cli")
    41	    if dispatch_mode is not None and isinstance(cli, Mapping):
    42	        dispatch_modes = cli.get("dispatch_modes")
    43	        if isinstance(dispatch_modes, Mapping):
    44	            mode = dispatch_modes.get(dispatch_mode)
    45	            if isinstance(mode, Mapping) and "isolation" in mode:
    46	                return cast(object, mode["isolation"])
    47	    return configured.get("isolation")
    48	
    49	
    50	def resolve_isolation(
    51	    *,
    52	    router_reachable: bool,
    53	    router_value: object | None,
    54	    configured_value: object | None,
    55	) -> IsolationResolution:
    56	    """Resolve router, configured, and default rungs without silent coercion."""
    57	    if router_reachable and router_value is not None:
    58	        return IsolationResolution(validate_isolation(router_value, rung="router"), "router")
    59	    if configured_value is not None:
    60	        return IsolationResolution(
    61	            validate_isolation(configured_value, rung="agents_yaml"), "agents_yaml"
    62	        )
    63	    return IsolationResolution("none", "default")

  1911	    """Return isolation for an exact agent/mode, or ``None`` if not found.
  1912	
  1913	    The legacy one-argument call retains first-type-match behavior. Callers
  1914	    that know the selected lane pass ``agent_id`` to avoid YAML-order coupling.
  1915	    """

   872	    def _resolve_args(self, args: list[str]) -> list[str]:
   873	        """Expand config placeholders in a mode's args.
   874	
   875	        The grok schema sentinel (``@review-findings-schema``) is replaced with
   876	        the schema derived from the canonical ``review-findings.schema.json``.
   877	        This is what keeps agents.yaml from carrying a hand-copied — and
   878	        drift-prone — ``--json-schema`` blob: the schema is injected here from
   879	        the single canonical file at dispatch time.
   880	
   881	        Raises :class:`SchemaInjectionError` when the schema cannot be resolved.
   882	        Dropping ``--json-schema`` and dispatching anyway used to look like
   883	        graceful degradation, but grok only populates ``structuredOutput`` when
   884	        that flag is present (see the agents.yaml comment on the review mode) —
   885	        so the "degraded" path reliably produced output the dispatcher then
   886	        rejected as invalid JSON, while the real cause (an unresolvable
   887	        canonical schema) appeared only as a warning. Failing here names the
   888	        actual problem.
   889	        """
   890	        mod = _schema_mod()
   891	        sentinel = getattr(mod, "GROK_SCHEMA_SENTINEL", "@review-findings-schema")
   892	        if sentinel not in args:
   893	            return list(args)
   894	
   895	        if mod is None:
   896	            raise SchemaInjectionError(
   897	                "review_findings_schema module could not be loaded, so the "
   898	                f"{sentinel!r} placeholder in agents.yaml cannot be resolved"
   899	            )
   900	        try:
   901	            schema_arg = mod.grok_schema_arg()
   902	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — re-raised with context
   903	            raise SchemaInjectionError(
   904	                f"could not derive the canonical review-findings schema: {exc}"
   905	            ) from exc
   906	
   907	        return [schema_arg if arg == sentinel else arg for arg in args]
   908	
   909	    def build_command(
   910	        self,
   911	        mode: str,
   912	        prompt: str,
   913	        model: str | None = None,
   914	        thinking: str | None = None,
   915	    ) -> list[str]:
   916	        """Build subprocess command from config.
   917	
   918	        When ``cli_config.prompt_via_stdin`` is True, the prompt is NOT
   919	        appended to the command — it will be passed via stdin instead.
   920	        When ``cli_config.prompt_via_flag`` is set, the prompt is attached as
   921	        the value of that flag (e.g. ``--prompt <prompt>``) and is neither a
   922	        trailing positional nor sent via stdin.
   923	
   924	        ``thinking`` is translated to vendor CLI flags from the authored
   925	        tier map (archetypes.yaml), not from hard-coded agents.yaml args.
   926	        """
   927	        mode_config = self.cli_config.dispatch_modes[mode]
   928	        cmd = [self.cli_config.command, *self._resolve_args(mode_config.args)]
   929	        # Drop any stale effort flags left in agents.yaml; tier thinking wins.
   930	        cmd = _strip_thinking_flags(self.vendor, cmd)
   931	        thinking_flags = _thinking_cli_flags(self.vendor, thinking)
   932	        if thinking_flags:
   933	            # Insert after the binary so mode flags still lead.
   934	            cmd[1:1] = thinking_flags
   935	        effective_model = model or self.cli_config.model
   936	        if effective_model:
   937	            cmd.extend([self.cli_config.model_flag, effective_model])
   938	        if self.cli_config.prompt_via_flag:
   939	            cmd.extend([self.cli_config.prompt_via_flag, prompt])
   940	        elif not self.cli_config.prompt_via_stdin:
   941	            cmd.append(prompt)
   942	        return cmd
   943	
   944	    def dispatch(
   945	        self,
   946	        mode: str,
   947	        prompt: str,
   948	        cwd: Path,
   949	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
   950	        archetype_model: str | None = None,
   951	        thinking: str | None = None,
   952	        repair_attempted: bool = False,
   953	        capacity_callback: Callable[[ReviewResult], Any] | None = None,
   954	    ) -> ReviewResult:
   955	        """Dispatch a review with model fallback on capacity errors.
   956	
   957	        Tries the primary model first, then each fallback in order.
   958	        Returns the first successful result or the final failure.
   959	
   960	        Args:

  2346	_GIT_INDEX_ERROR_MARKERS = (
  2347	    "index.lock",
  2348	    "unable to access index",
  2349	    "another git process",
  2350	)

  2353	def _is_concurrent_git_error(result: ReviewResult) -> bool:
  2354	    """True when a vendor CLI failed because of concurrent git index access."""
  2355	    blob = "\n".join(
  2356	        part for part in (result.error, result.raw_stderr, result.raw_stdout) if part
  2357	    ).lower()
  2358	    return any(marker in blob for marker in _GIT_INDEX_ERROR_MARKERS)

  2361	def _safe_path_component(value: str) -> str:
  2362	    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", value).strip("._-")
  2363	    return cleaned or "unknown"

  2373	def _main_repo_from_cwd(cwd: Path) -> Path:
  2374	    """Resolve the main repository root even when *cwd* is a linked worktree."""
  2375	    try:
  2376	        proc = subprocess.run(
  2377	            ["git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"],
  2378	            cwd=str(cwd),
  2379	            capture_output=True,
  2380	            text=True,
  2381	            timeout=15,
  2382	        )
  2383	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2384	        return Path(cwd)
  2385	    if proc.returncode != 0 or not proc.stdout.strip():
  2386	        return Path(cwd)
  2387	    git_common = proc.stdout.strip()
  2388	    if git_common == ".git":
  2389	        try:
  2390	            top = subprocess.run(
  2391	                ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
  2392	                cwd=str(cwd),
  2393	                capture_output=True,
  2394	                text=True,
  2395	                timeout=15,
  2396	            )
  2397	        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2398	            return Path(cwd)
  2399	        if top.returncode == 0 and top.stdout.strip():
  2400	            return Path(top.stdout.strip())
  2401	        return Path(cwd)
  2402	    common_path = Path(git_common)
  2403	    if not common_path.is_absolute():
  2404	        common_path = (Path(cwd) / common_path).resolve()
  2405	    if common_path.name == ".git":
  2406	        return common_path.parent
  2407	    return common_path

  2410	def review_snapshot_path(cwd: Path, round_id: str, vendor: str) -> Path:
  2411	    """``.git-worktrees/.review-snapshots/<round>/<vendor>/`` under the main repo."""
  2412	    root = _main_repo_from_cwd(cwd) / ".git-worktrees" / ".review-snapshots"
  2413	    return root / _safe_path_component(round_id) / _safe_path_component(vendor)

  2416	def create_review_snapshot(cwd: Path, round_id: str, vendor: str) -> Path:
  2417	    """Add a detached throwaway worktree for one vendor retry, then return it."""
  2418	    dest = review_snapshot_path(cwd, round_id, vendor)
  2419	    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  2420	    if dest.exists():
  2421	        destroy_review_snapshot(dest, cwd)
  2422	    subprocess.run(
  2423	        ["git", "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(dest), "HEAD"],
  2424	        cwd=str(cwd),
  2425	        check=True,
  2426	        capture_output=True,
  2427	        text=True,
  2428	        timeout=60,
  2429	    )
  2430	    return dest
  2431

  2433	def destroy_review_snapshot(snapshot: Path, git_cwd: Path) -> None:
  2434	    """Remove a review snapshot worktree after collect. Best-effort."""
  2435	    try:
  2436	        subprocess.run(
  2437	            ["git", "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(snapshot)],
  2438	            cwd=str(git_cwd),
  2439	            capture_output=True,
  2440	            text=True,
  2441	            timeout=60,
  2442	            check=False,
  2443	        )
  2444	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
  2445	        logger.warning("Failed to remove review snapshot %s: %s", snapshot, exc)
  2446	    if Path(snapshot).exists():
  2447	        shutil.rmtree(snapshot, ignore_errors=True)
  2448	    try:
  2449	        subprocess.run(
  2450	            ["git", "worktree", "prune"],
  2451	            cwd=str(git_cwd),
  2452	            capture_output=True,
  2453	            text=True,
  2454	            timeout=30,
  2455	            check=False,
  2456	        )
  2457	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2458	        pass

  2460	
  2461	def _dispatch_with_snapshot_fallback(
  2462	    *,
  2463	    vendor: str,
  2464	    cwd: Path,
  2465	    round_id: str,
  2466	    run: Callable[[Path], ReviewResult],
  2467	) -> ReviewResult:
  2468	    """Run *run(cwd)*; on concurrent git-index failure, retry on a snapshot."""
  2469	    result = run(cwd)
  2470	    if result.success or not _is_concurrent_git_error(result):
  2471	        return result
  2472	    logger.warning(
  2473	        "Concurrent git access error for %s; retrying on detached snapshot",
  2474	        vendor,
  2475	    )
  2476	    snapshot: Path | None = None
  2477	    try:
  2478	        snapshot = create_review_snapshot(cwd, round_id, vendor)
  2479	        return run(snapshot)
  2480	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — keep the original vendor error
  2481	        logger.warning("Snapshot fallback failed for %s: %s", vendor, exc)
  2482	        return result
  2483	    finally:
  2484	        if snapshot is not None:
  2485	            destroy_review_snapshot(snapshot, cwd)

  2706	        """Discover the agent-coordinator directory from MCP config.
  2707	
  2708	        Reads ``~/.claude.json`` to find the coordination MCP server's
  2709	        ``run_mcp.py`` path, then derives the agent-coordinator directory
  2710	        and Python binary from it.  Returns ``(python_bin, ac_dir)`` or
  2711	        ``None`` if not configured.

  2713	        claude_json = Path.home() / ".claude.json"
  2714	        if not claude_json.is_file():

  2717	            cfg = json.loads(claude_json.read_text())
  2718	            mcp = cfg.get("mcpServers", {}).get("coordination", {})
  2719	            python_bin = mcp.get("command", "")
  2720	            args = mcp.get("args", [])
  2721	            if not python_bin or not args:
  2722	                return None
  2723	            # args[0] is the path to run_mcp.py; its parent is agent-coordinator
  2724	            ac_dir = Path(args[0]).resolve().parent
  2725	            if not ac_dir.is_dir():
  2726	                return None
  2727	            return (python_bin, ac_dir)
  2728	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError, IndexError):
  2729	            return None

   508	
   509	def classify_error(text: str) -> ErrorClass:
   510	    """Classify a vendor error from its output text.
   511	
   512	    Accepts stderr OR stdout — some CLIs (pi) exit 0 with the provider's
   513	    error body on stdout (issue #383), so classification cannot assume the
   514	    text arrived on stderr. UNAVAILABLE is checked first: a billing body
   515	    ("Insufficient credits … upgrade your limit") contains words that would
   516	    otherwise false-positive the capacity patterns.
   517	    """
   518	    lower = text.lower()
   519	    if any(p in lower for p in _UNAVAILABLE_PATTERNS) or _UNAVAILABLE_402_RE.search(lower):
   520	        return ErrorClass.UNAVAILABLE
   521	    if any(p in lower for p in _AUTH_PATTERNS):
   522	        return ErrorClass.AUTH
   523	    if any(p in lower for p in _CAPACITY_PATTERNS):
   524	        return ErrorClass.CAPACITY
   525	    if any(p in lower for p in _TRANSIENT_PATTERNS):
   526	        return ErrorClass.TRANSIENT
   527	    return ErrorClass.UNKNOWN

  2706	        """Discover the agent-coordinator directory from MCP config.
  2707	
  2708	        Reads ``~/.claude.json`` to find the coordination MCP server's

  2718	            mcp = cfg.get("mcpServers", {}).get("coordination", {})
  2719	            python_bin = mcp.get("command", "")
  2720	            args = mcp.get("args", [])
  2721	            if not python_bin or not args:
  2722	                return None
  2723	            # args[0] is the path to run_mcp.py; its parent is agent-coordinator
  2724	            ac_dir = Path(args[0]).resolve().parent
  2725	            if not ac_dir.is_dir():
  2726	                return None

  2731	    @classmethod
  2732	    def from_coordinator(cls) -> "ReviewOrchestrator":
  2733	        """Create orchestrator using provider-neutral discovery order."""
  2734	        explicit = cls._explicit_agents_yaml_path()
  2735	        if explicit:
  2736	            data = cls._config_from_agents_yaml(explicit)
  2737	            if data is not None:
  2738	                return cls.from_config_dict(data)
  2739	
  2740	        data = cls._load_from_http()
  2741	        if data is not None:
  2742	            return cls.from_config_dict(data)
  2743	
  2744	        # Provider-native fallback. Today this includes Claude Code MCP config.
  2745	        found = cls._find_coordinator_dir()
  2746	        if found:
  2747	            python_bin, ac_dir = found
  2748	            script = ac_dir / "get_dispatch_configs.py"
  2749	            if script.is_file():
  2750	                try:
  2751	                    result = subprocess.run(
  2752	                        [python_bin, str(script)],
  2753	                        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15,
  2754	                    )
  2755	                    if result.returncode == 0:
  2756	                        return cls.from_config_dict(json.loads(result.stdout))
  2757	                    logger.warning("Coordinator query failed: %s", result.stderr[:200])
  2758	                except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
  2759	                    logger.warning("Coordinator query error: %s", exc)
  2760	
  2761	        # Compatibility only: source-repository configuration is considered
  2762	        # after explicit, HTTP, and provider-native MCP configuration.
  2763	        local = cls._find_local_agents_yaml()
  2764	        if local:
  2765	            data = cls._config_from_agents_yaml(local)
  2766	            if data is not None:
  2767	                return cls.from_config_dict(data)
  2768	
  2769	        logger.warning("No public or local vendor configuration found")
  2770	        return cls({})

    11	# The review_type (plan vs implementation) determines what is being
    12	# reviewed/generated; the dispatch mode controls sandbox permissions.
    13	#
    14	# The optional `sdk` section configures SDK-based API dispatch as a
    15	# fallback when the vendor's CLI is not installed.  API keys are resolved
    16	# via OpenBao at runtime (using `openbao_role_id`), falling back to the
    17	# environment variable named in `api_key_env`.
    18	#
    19	# The optional `archetypes` field declares which agent archetypes (defined in
    20	# archetypes.yaml) this agent can fulfill. When set, the coordinator work
    21	# queue filters claims by archetype compatibility — a task submitted with
    22	# `agent_requirements.archetype = "architect"` will only be claimed by agents
    23	# whose archetypes list includes "architect". Agents with no archetypes
    24	# field (or an empty list) are backward-compatible and can claim any task.
    25	#
    26	# Because that filter is exact, an archetype rostered in teams.yaml but absent
    27	# from every agent's list here is UNCLAIMABLE: a task submitted for it sits
    28	# pending forever, with no error — the queue has nothing to reject, it simply
    29	# never matches (issue #390). `CrewManifest.validate_against` now cross-checks
    30	# this file against the roster and fails loud on such a role, so keep the two
    31	# in sync: adding a roster entry to teams.yaml means giving at least one agent
    32	# of an eligible vendor that archetype here.
    33	
    34	# vendor_diversity policy: when a worker (implementer) and a validator (reviewer
    35	# or behavioral validator) are dispatched to the same OpenSpec change, the
    36	# dispatcher selects them from different vendors. This avoids shared
    37	# training-data biases between the agent that wrote the code and the agent that
    38	# reviews it — a validator with the same training distribution is more likely
    39	# to confirm the worker's design choices than to challenge them.
    40	#
    41	# When only one vendor is available (single-vendor environment, or rate limits
    42	# exhausted alternatives), the dispatcher logs a warning and continues with the
    43	# single vendor (fallback: warn_and_continue). The policy can be disabled by
    44	# setting `enforce_for` to an empty list. Scope `per_change` means the
    45	# constraint applies across all packages within one OpenSpec change.
    46	policies:
    47	  vendor_diversity:
    48	    enforce_for: [worker_vs_validator]
    49	    fallback: warn_and_continue
    50	    scope: per_change

  2461	def _dispatch_with_snapshot_fallback(
  2462	    *,
  2463	    vendor: str,
  2464	    cwd: Path,
  2465	    round_id: str,
  2466	    run: Callable[[Path], ReviewResult],
  2467	) -> ReviewResult:
  2468	    """Run *run(cwd)*; on concurrent git-index failure, retry on a snapshot."""
  2469	    result = run(cwd)
  2470	    if result.success or not _is_concurrent_git_error(result):
  2471	        return result
  2472	    logger.warning(
  2473	        "Concurrent git access error for %s; retrying on detached snapshot",
  2474	        vendor,
  2475	    )
  2476	    snapshot: Path | None = None
  2477	    try:
  2478	        snapshot = create_review_snapshot(cwd, round_id, vendor)
  2479	        return run(snapshot)
  2480	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — keep the original vendor error
  2481	        logger.warning("Snapshot fallback failed for %s: %s", vendor, exc)
  2482	        return result
  2483	    finally:
  2484	        if snapshot is not None:
  2485	            destroy_review_snapshot(snapshot, cwd)
  2486

  2493	    """Multi-vendor review dispatch orchestrator.
  2494	
  2495	    Supports CLI, SDK, and OpenAI-compatible adapters with ordered selection:
  2496	    Tier 1 (Local CLI) → Tier 2 (SDK/API) → Tier 2.5 (OpenAI-compatible)
  2497	    → Tier 3 (Skip).
  2498	    """

     1	"""Provider-neutral autopilot phase dispatch adapters.
     2	
     3	Scope note for the built-in `local` adapter: its concurrency cap
     4	(``LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY``) is enforced **per process**, not host-wide.
     5	The gate is a :class:`threading.Semaphore` owned by this module, so N concurrent
     6	autopilot processes pointed at the same endpoint can each admit up to the cap —
     7	the endpoint may see N x cap simultaneous requests. Host-level admission control
     8	belongs to the serving stack in front of the GPU, not here.

    38	@dataclass
    39	class PhaseDispatchPayload:
    40	    schema_version: int
    41	    change_id: str
    42	    phase: str
    43	    provider: str
    44	    archetype: str | None
    45	    model: str | None
    46	    prompt: str
    47	    system_prompt: str | None
    48	    isolation: str | None
    49	    expected_outcomes: list[str]
    50	    agent_id: str | None = None
    51	
    52	    @classmethod
    53	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "PhaseDispatchPayload":
    54	        return cls(
    55	            schema_version=int(data.get("schema_version", 1)),
    56	            change_id=str(data["change_id"]),
    57	            phase=str(data["phase"]),
    58	            provider=str(data["provider"]),
    59	            archetype=data.get("archetype"),
    60	            model=data.get("model"),
    61	            prompt=str(data["prompt"]),
    62	            system_prompt=data.get("system_prompt"),
    63	            isolation=data.get("isolation"),
    64	            expected_outcomes=list(data.get("expected_outcomes") or []),
    65	            agent_id=data.get("agent_id"),
    66	        )
    67	
    68	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    69	        return asdict(self)

    76	    handoff_id: str = ""
    77	    provider: str = ""
    78	    model_used: str | None = None
    79	    dispatch_tier: str = "fallback"
    80	    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    81	    agent_id: str | None = None
    82	    error_class: str | None = None
    83	    capacity_scope: str | None = None
    84	    capacity_model: str | None = None
    85	    capacity_reset_at: str | None = None
    86	    capacity_retry_after_seconds: int | None = None
    87	
    88	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    89	        return asdict(self)

    92	ProviderRunner = Callable[[PhaseDispatchPayload], Any]
    93	
    94	_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS = {"claude_code", "codex", "antigravity", "grok", "pi", "local"}
    95	_CLAUDE_ALIASES = {"opus", "sonnet", "haiku", "fable"}
    96	
    97	# --- local provider adapter (OpenSpec add-local-model-provider-tier, D2/D5) ---
    98	#
    99	# `local` launches the existing Pi coding-agent harness with its normal file and
   100	# command tools. A one-shot Pi extension registers the distinct `local` provider
   101	# against the operator-run OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-server / vLLM /
   102	# Ollama); stdlib urllib remains only for the bounded health probe.
   103	#
   104	# Environment contract:
   105	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL       required to enable; http:// or https:// only;
   106	#                                  includes the API version prefix, e.g.
   107	#                                  "http://gx10.local:8080/v1"
   108	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_API_KEY        optional bearer token
   109	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY  optional, default 4, clamped to 64; excess
   110	#                                  dispatches queue (per process — see the module
   111	#                                  docstring)
   112	#
   113	# With LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL unset the provider is inert: dispatch returns the
   114	# same structured `fallback` result any unconfigured adapter returns, and no
   115	# network call is made (Rule 4 — safe default).
   116	_LOCAL_PROVIDER = "local"
   117	_LOCAL_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 4
   118	# A process cannot usefully hold more in-flight local requests than this, and a
   119	# fat-fingered env value must not turn the gate into an unbounded thread farm.
   120	_LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 64
   121	# Only these schemes are dispatchable; anything else (file:, ftp:, a bare host)
   122	# is a misconfiguration, not an endpoint.
   123	_LOCAL_ALLOWED_SCHEMES = ("http", "https")
   124	# Short by design: a dead endpoint must surface as adapter unavailability in
   125	# seconds, never as a stalled phase.
   126	_LOCAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 3.0
   127	# Bounded wall-clock ceiling for the headless Pi agent process.
   128	_LOCAL_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300
   129	# Upper bound on time spent queued behind the concurrency cap. Queueing is
   130	# required by the spec (excess dispatches queue, they are never dropped), but it
   131	# must still terminate: a wedged slot holder degrades the waiter to the
   132	# structured fallback instead of parking the phase forever.
   133	_LOCAL_GATE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 1800
   134	# The probe verdict is a cache, not a fact. A short TTL keeps a restarted or
   135	# just-crashed endpoint from being pinned to a stale verdict for the whole
   136	# process lifetime, in either direction.
   137	_LOCAL_PROBE_TTL_SECONDS = 30.0
   138	# Responses are JSON handoffs, not model weights: anything past this budget is a
   139	# misbehaving endpoint and fails closed to the structured fallback.
   140	_LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024
   141	_LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION = Path(__file__).with_name("pi_local_provider.ts")
   142	# Defence in depth for the resolver-side trust boundary (design D3). The
   143	# coordinator is the single decision point, but a payload can reach this adapter
   144	# from any client; an archetype outside this allowlist never reaches the wire.
   145	_LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES = frozenset({"runner", "analyst", "documenter", "validator"})
   146	
   147	
   148	class LocalAdapterError(RuntimeError):
   149	    """Base for adapter-side local failures. Never escapes ``dispatch_phase``."""
   150	
   151	
   152	class LocalDeadlineExceeded(LocalAdapterError, TimeoutError):
   153	    """The HTTP health probe exceeded its wall-clock deadline."""
   154	
   155	
   156	class LocalGateTimeout(LocalAdapterError, TimeoutError):
   157	    """Waiting for a concurrency slot blew its bound."""
   158	
   159	
   160	class LocalResponseTooLarge(LocalAdapterError, ValueError):
   161	    """The endpoint sent more bytes than the response budget allows."""
   162	
   163	
   164	_local_state_lock = threading.Lock()
   165	# Serializes cold probes so concurrent first-callers issue one request, not N.
   166	_local_probe_lock = threading.Lock()
   167	# (base_url, reachable, expires_at_monotonic) — TTL'd, and invalidated whenever a
   168	# dispatch hits a connection error.
   169	_local_probe_cache: tuple[str, bool, float] | None = None
   170	_local_gate_semaphore: threading.Semaphore | None = None
   171	_local_gate_limit: int | None = None
   172	
   173	
   174	def reset_local_adapter_state() -> None:
   175	    """Drop the cached health probe and concurrency gate (test hook)."""
   176	    global _local_probe_cache, _local_gate_semaphore, _local_gate_limit
   177	    with _local_state_lock:
   178	        _local_probe_cache = None
   179	        _local_gate_semaphore = None
   180	        _local_gate_limit = None
   181	
   182	
   183	def invalidate_local_probe_cache() -> None:
   184	    """Forget the cached probe verdict; the next caller re-probes."""
   185	    global _local_probe_cache
   186	    with _local_state_lock:
   187	        _local_probe_cache = None
   188	
   189	
   190	class _ReadableResponse(Protocol):
   191	    def read(self, amount: int = -1) -> bytes: ...
   192	
   193	
   194	def _read_capped(resp: _ReadableResponse) -> bytes:
   195	    """Read at most :data:`_LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` from *resp*, else fail."""
   196	    chunk = resp.read(_LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES + 1)
   197	    if len(chunk) > _LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES:
   198	        raise LocalResponseTooLarge(
   199	            f"response exceeded the {_LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES}-byte budget"
   200	        )
   201	    return chunk
   202	
   203	
   204	def _http_get_json(url: str, headers: dict[str, str], timeout: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
   205	    """Real HTTP GET transport used only by the bounded health probe."""
   206	    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers, method="GET")
   207	    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:  # noqa: S310
   208	        parsed: Any = json.loads(_read_capped(resp).decode("utf-8"))
   209	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
   210	        raise LocalAdapterError("local health probe returned a non-object body")
   211	    return parsed
   212	
   213	
   214	def _call_with_deadline(fn: Callable[[], Any], deadline_seconds: float) -> Any:
   215	    """Run *fn* under a wall-clock deadline.
   216	
   217	    ``urllib``'s ``timeout`` is per socket operation: an endpoint that trickles a
   218	    byte every few seconds never trips it. A bounded worker gives probe and
   219	    dispatch a real ceiling — the caller is released at the deadline (freeing its
   220	    concurrency slot) while the abandoned request is left to the daemon thread.
   220	    concurrency slot) while the abandoned request is left to the daemon thread.
   221	    """
   222	    box: dict[str, Any] = {}
   223	
   224	    def _run() -> None:
   225	        try:
   226	            box["value"] = fn()
   227	        except BaseException as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — re-raised in the caller
   228	            box["error"] = exc
   229	
   230	    worker = threading.Thread(target=_run, daemon=True)
   231	    worker.start()
   232	    worker.join(deadline_seconds)
   233	    if worker.is_alive():
   234	        raise LocalDeadlineExceeded(
   235	            f"local endpoint did not answer within {deadline_seconds}s"
   236	        )
   237	    if "error" in box:
   238	        raise box["error"]
   239	    return box.get("value")
   240	
   241	
   242	def _is_connection_error(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
   243	    """Whether *exc* casts doubt on endpoint reachability (probe invalidation)."""
   244	    return isinstance(exc, (OSError, LocalDeadlineExceeded, LocalGateTimeout))
   245	
   246	
   247	def _local_base_url_raw() -> str:
   248	    return os.environ.get("LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL", "").strip().rstrip("/")
   249	
   250	
   251	def _local_base_url() -> str | None:
   252	    """The configured endpoint, or None when unset or not an http(s) URL."""
   253	    raw = _local_base_url_raw()
   254	    if not raw:
   255	        return None
   256	    if urllib.parse.urlsplit(raw).scheme.lower() not in _LOCAL_ALLOWED_SCHEMES:
   257	        return None
   258	    return raw
   259	
   260	
   261	def _local_headers() -> dict[str, str]:
   262	    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
   263	    api_key = os.environ.get("LOCAL_INFERENCE_API_KEY", "").strip()
   264	    if api_key:
   265	        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"
   266	    return headers
   267	
   268	
   269	def _local_max_concurrency() -> int:
   270	    """Simultaneous local dispatches; anything unparseable or <=0 uses the default."""
   271	    try:
   272	        value = int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY", "").strip())
   273	    except ValueError:
   274	        return _LOCAL_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY
   275	    if value <= 0:
   276	        return _LOCAL_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY
   277	    if value > _LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY:
   278	        logger.warning(
   279	            "LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY=%s clamped to %s",
   280	            value,
   281	            _LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY,
   282	        )
   283	        return _LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY
   284	    return value
   285	
   286	
   287	def _local_gate() -> threading.Semaphore:
   288	    """Concurrency cap. Excess dispatches block (queue), they are never dropped.
   289	
   290	    The cap is read from the environment exactly once (first use, or after
   291	    :func:`reset_local_adapter_state`). Re-reading it per dispatch would let a
   292	    mid-run env change swap the semaphore out from under in-flight holders, and
   293	    the new gate would admit its full limit on top of them.
   294	    """
   295	    global _local_gate_semaphore, _local_gate_limit
   296	    with _local_state_lock:
   297	        if _local_gate_semaphore is None:
   298	            _local_gate_limit = _local_max_concurrency()
   299	            _local_gate_semaphore = threading.Semaphore(_local_gate_limit)
   300	        return _local_gate_semaphore
   301	
   302	
   303	def _cached_probe_verdict(base_url: str) -> bool | None:
   304	    """The unexpired cached verdict for *base_url*, or None when it must re-probe."""
   305	    with _local_state_lock:
   306	        cached = _local_probe_cache
   307	    if cached is None or cached[0] != base_url:
   308	        return None
   309	    if time.monotonic() >= cached[2]:
   310	        return None
   311	    return cached[1]
   312	
   313	
   314	def local_endpoint_available(*, force: bool = False) -> bool:
   315	    """Whether the configured local endpoint answered its health probe.
   316	
   317	    Probes ``GET {LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL}/models`` (the OpenAI-compatible model
   318	    listing) with a short timeout and caches the verdict for
   319	    :data:`_LOCAL_PROBE_TTL_SECONDS`. The TTL matters in both directions: a
   320	    single transient failure must not blackhole `local` for the rest of the
   321	    process, and an endpoint that dies after one good probe must not stay
   322	    "available" forever. A dispatch-time connection error additionally
   323	    invalidates the cache immediately.
   324	
   325	    Returns False when no endpoint is configured, or when the configured value is
   326	    not an http(s) URL — callers (dispatch, and the roadmap policy engine's
   327	    switch-target selection) treat that as "adapter unavailable", never an error.
   328	    """
   329	    global _local_probe_cache
   330	    base_url = _local_base_url()
   331	    if base_url is None:
   332	        raw = _local_base_url_raw()
   333	        if raw:
   334	            logger.warning(
   335	                "local adapter unavailable: LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL must use one "
   336	                "of %s (got scheme %r)",
   337	                "/".join(_LOCAL_ALLOWED_SCHEMES),
   338	                urllib.parse.urlsplit(raw).scheme,
   339	            )
   340	        return False
   341	
   342	    if not force:
   343	        cached = _cached_probe_verdict(base_url)
   344	        if cached is not None:
   345	            return cached
   346	
   347	    # Single-flight: concurrent cold callers collapse onto one probe.
   348	    with _local_probe_lock:
   349	        if not force:
   350	            cached = _cached_probe_verdict(base_url)
   351	            if cached is not None:
   352	                return cached
   353	        try:
   354	            _call_with_deadline(
   355	                lambda: _http_get_json(
   356	                    f"{base_url}/models",
   357	                    _local_headers(),
   358	                    _LOCAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   359	                ),
   360	                _LOCAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   361	            )
   362	            reachable = True
   363	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — any probe failure is unavailability
   364	            logger.debug("local health probe failed for %s: %s", base_url, exc)
   365	            reachable = False
   366	
   367	        with _local_state_lock:
   368	            _local_probe_cache = (
   369	                base_url,
   370	                reachable,
   371	                time.monotonic() + _LOCAL_PROBE_TTL_SECONDS,
   372	            )
   373	        return reachable
   374	
   375	
   376	def normalize_dispatch_result(
   377	    raw: Any,
   378	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   379	    dispatch_tier: str,
   380	) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   381	    """Normalize tuple/dict adapter output into the contract result shape."""
   382	    warnings: list[str] = []
   383	    outcome: str | None = None
   384	    handoff_id: str | None = None
   385	    model_used = payload.model
   386	    error_class: str | None = None
   387	    capacity_scope: str | None = None
   388	    capacity_model: str | None = None
   389	    capacity_reset_at: str | None = None
   390	    capacity_retry_after_seconds: int | None = None
   391	
   392	    if isinstance(raw, tuple) and len(raw) == 2:
   393	        outcome, handoff_id = raw
   394	    elif isinstance(raw, dict):
   395	        outcome = raw.get("outcome")
   396	        handoff_id = raw.get("handoff_id")
   397	        model_used = raw.get("model_used", model_used)
   398	        error_class = raw.get("error_class")
   399	        capacity_scope = raw.get("capacity_scope")
   400	        capacity_model = raw.get("capacity_model")
   401	        capacity_reset_at = raw.get("capacity_reset_at")
   402	        capacity_retry_after_seconds = raw.get("capacity_retry_after_seconds")
   403	        raw_warnings = raw.get("warnings")
   404	        if isinstance(raw_warnings, list):
   405	            warnings = [str(item) for item in raw_warnings]
   406	
   407	    if not isinstance(outcome, str) or not outcome:
   408	        outcome = "failed"
   409	        warnings.append("adapter returned missing outcome")
   410	    if not isinstance(handoff_id, str) or not handoff_id:
   411	        digest = hashlib.sha256(
   412	            json.dumps(payload.to_dict(), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
   413	        ).hexdigest()[:12]
   414	        handoff_id = f"{dispatch_tier}:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:{digest}"
   415	        warnings.append("adapter returned missing handoff_id")
   416	
   417	    return PhaseDispatchResult(
   418	        outcome=outcome,
   419	        handoff_id=handoff_id,
   420	        provider=payload.provider,
   421	        model_used=model_used,
   422	        dispatch_tier=dispatch_tier,
   423	        warnings=warnings,
   424	        agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   425	        error_class=error_class,
   426	        capacity_scope=capacity_scope,
   427	        capacity_model=capacity_model,
   428	        capacity_reset_at=capacity_reset_at,
   429	        capacity_retry_after_seconds=capacity_retry_after_seconds,
   430	    )
   431	
   432	
   433	def _fallback_result(
   434	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   435	    warning: str,
   436	) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   437	    """The structured degradation every unconfigured adapter returns."""
   438	    return PhaseDispatchResult(
   439	        outcome="failed",
   440	        handoff_id=f"fallback:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}",
   441	        provider=payload.provider,
   442	        model_used=payload.model,
   443	        dispatch_tier="fallback",
   444	        warnings=[warning],
   445	        agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   446	    )

   449	def _local_harness_prompt(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> str:
   450	    """Build the phase prompt consumed by the tool-capable Pi agent harness."""
   451	    expected = ", ".join(payload.expected_outcomes) or "complete, failed"
   452	    result_contract = json.dumps(
   453	        {
   454	            "outcome": f"<one of: {expected}>",
   455	            "handoff_id": "<real handoff id>",
   456	        },
   457	        separators=(",", ":"),
   458	    )
   459	    sections = [
   460	        payload.system_prompt or "You are a focused phase agent.",
   461	        payload.prompt,
   462	        (
   463	            "Use the coding-agent tools to inspect files, run commands, and make "
   464	            "only the changes required by this phase. A text-only answer is not a "
   465	            "completed phase. Before finishing, write a durable handoff through the "
   466	            "configured coordinator handoff capability (or its documented local "
   467	            "fallback). Your final assistant message must be only this JSON shape: "
   468	            f"{result_contract}. Never invent or omit the handoff id."
   469	        ),
   470	    ]
   471	    return (chr(10) * 2).join(sections)
   472	
   473	
   474	def _run_local_agent_cli(
   475	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   476	) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
   477	    """Run Pi headlessly with the local endpoint registered as a provider."""
   478	    if not _LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION.is_file():
   479	        raise LocalAdapterError("local Pi provider extension is missing")
   480	    env = os.environ.copy()
   481	    env["LOCAL_INFERENCE_MODEL"] = payload.model or ""
   482	    command = [
   483	        "pi",
   484	        "-p",
   485	        "--provider",
   486	        "local",
   487	        "--model",
   488	        payload.model or "",
   489	        "--mode",
   490	        "json",
   491	        "--approve",
   492	        "--no-session",
   493	        "--extension",
   494	        str(_LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION),
   495	        _local_harness_prompt(payload),
   496	    ]
   497	    return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 -- fixed executable and list-form args
   498	        command,
   499	        capture_output=True,
   500	        text=True,
   501	        timeout=_LOCAL_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   502	        env=env,
   503	        check=False,
   504	    )
   505	
   506	
   507	def _assistant_text(message: Any) -> str | None:
   508	    """Extract assistant text from a Pi JSON-mode message payload."""
   509	    if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") != "assistant":
   510	        return None
   511	    content = message.get("content")
   512	    if isinstance(content, str):
   513	        return content
   514	    if isinstance(content, list):
   515	        parts = [
   516	            part["text"]
   517	            for part in content
   518	            if isinstance(part, dict) and isinstance(part.get("text"), str)
   519	        ]
   520	        return chr(10).join(parts) if parts else None
   521	    return None
   522	
   523	
   524	def _parse_local_harness_output(stdout: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   525	    """Return the last explicit outcome and handoff id from Pi NDJSON."""
   526	    last_text: str | None = None
   527	    for line in stdout.splitlines():
   528	        try:
   529	            event = json.loads(line)
   530	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
   531	            continue
   532	        if not isinstance(event, dict):
   533	            continue
   534	        text = _assistant_text(event.get("message"))
   535	        if text:
   536	            last_text = text
   537	    if last_text is None:
   538	        return None
   539	    try:
   540	        parsed = json.loads(last_text)
   540	        parsed = json.loads(last_text)
   541	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
   542	        return None
   543	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
   544	        return None
   545	    outcome = parsed.get("outcome")
   546	    handoff_id = parsed.get("handoff_id")
   547	    if (
   548	        not isinstance(outcome, str)
   549	        or not outcome.strip()
   550	        or not isinstance(handoff_id, str)
   551	        or not handoff_id.strip()
   552	    ):
   553	        return None
   554	    return parsed
   555	
   556	
   557	def _local_runner(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> dict[str, Any]:
   558	    """Run one capped tool-capable agent session against the local endpoint."""
   559	    gate = _local_gate()
   560	    if not gate.acquire(timeout=_LOCAL_GATE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):
   561	        raise LocalGateTimeout(
   562	            f"no local dispatch slot within {_LOCAL_GATE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s"
   563	        )
   564	    try:
   565	        completed = _run_local_agent_cli(payload)
   566	    finally:
   567	        gate.release()
   568	
   569	    if completed.returncode != 0:
   570	        return {
   571	            "outcome": "failed",
   572	            "warnings": ["local agent harness exited non-zero"],
   573	        }
   574	    if len(completed.stdout.encode("utf-8")) > _LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES:
   575	        raise LocalResponseTooLarge("local agent harness output exceeded byte budget")
   576	    result = _parse_local_harness_output(completed.stdout)
   577	    if result is None:
   578	        return {
   579	            "outcome": "failed",
   580	            "warnings": [
   581	                "local agent harness returned no explicit outcome and real handoff_id"
   582	            ],
   583	        }
   584	    if payload.expected_outcomes and result["outcome"] not in payload.expected_outcomes:
   585	        return {
   586	            "outcome": "failed",
   587	            "warnings": ["local agent harness returned an unexpected outcome"],
   588	        }
   589	    return result
   590	
   591	
   592	def _local_trust_boundary_warning(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> str | None:
   593	    """Refusal reason when *payload*'s archetype may not be served by `local`.
   594	
   595	    Design D3 puts the trust boundary in the coordinator's resolver. This is the
   596	    adapter-side backstop for payloads that never went through it: an absent or
   597	    non-permitted archetype is refused here, before any request is built.
   598	    """
   599	    archetype = payload.archetype
   600	    permitted = ", ".join(sorted(_LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES))
   601	    if not isinstance(archetype, str) or not archetype:
   602	        return (
   603	            "payload carries no archetype, so the 'local' provider trust boundary "
   604	            f"cannot be satisfied (permitted: {permitted}); no dispatch attempted"
   605	        )
   606	    if archetype not in _LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES:
   607	        return (
   608	            f"archetype {archetype!r} is outside the 'local' provider trust "
   609	            f"boundary (permitted: {permitted}); no dispatch attempted"
   610	        )
   611	    return None
   612	
   613	
   614	def _dispatch_local(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   615	    """Dispatch through the built-in local adapter, degrading instead of raising."""
   616	    if _local_base_url() is None:
   617	        if _local_base_url_raw():
   618	            return _fallback_result(
   619	                payload,
   620	                "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL "
   621	                "must be an http:// or https:// URL",
   622	            )
   623	        return _fallback_result(
   624	            payload,
   625	            "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL is not set",
   626	        )
   627	    boundary = _local_trust_boundary_warning(payload)
   628	    if boundary is not None:
   629	        return _fallback_result(
   630	            payload, f"adapter unavailable for provider 'local': {boundary}"
   631	        )
   632	    if not payload.model:
   633	        return _fallback_result(
   634	            payload,
   635	            "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': no model resolved for this "
   636	            "phase; no dispatch attempted",
   637	        )
   638	    if not local_endpoint_available():
   639	        return _fallback_result(
   640	            payload,
   641	            "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': health probe failed for "
   642	            "the configured endpoint",
   643	        )
   644	    try:
   645	        raw = _local_runner(payload)
   646	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — a dead endpoint must not fail the phase
   647	        logger.debug("local dispatch failed", exc_info=True)
   648	        if _is_connection_error(exc):
   649	            # The cached "reachable" verdict is now suspect; make the next
   650	            # caller re-probe instead of retrying into a black hole.
   651	            invalidate_local_probe_cache()
   652	        return _fallback_result(
   653	            payload,
   654	            "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': dispatch failed "
   655	            f"({type(exc).__name__})",
   656	        )
   657	    return normalize_dispatch_result(raw, payload, "harness")
   658	
   659	
   660	def _dry_run_result(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   661	    if payload.provider != "claude_code" and payload.model in _CLAUDE_ALIASES:
   662	        return PhaseDispatchResult(
   663	            outcome="failed",
   664	            handoff_id=f"dry-run:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:invalid-model",
   665	            provider=payload.provider,
   666	            model_used=payload.model,
   667	            dispatch_tier="dry_run",
   668	            agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   669	            warnings=[
   670	                f"Claude alias {payload.model!r} is not valid for provider {payload.provider!r}",
   671	            ],
   672	        )
   673	    if payload.provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER:
   674	        # Dry run models the real decision path: a payload the adapter would
   675	        # refuse at the trust boundary must not dry-run "complete".
   676	        boundary = _local_trust_boundary_warning(payload)
   677	        if boundary is not None:
   678	            return PhaseDispatchResult(
   679	                outcome="failed",
   680	                handoff_id=f"dry-run:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:trust-boundary",
   681	                provider=payload.provider,
   682	                model_used=payload.model,
   683	                dispatch_tier="dry_run",
   684	                warnings=[f"dispatch would be refused for provider 'local': {boundary}"],
   685	            )
   686	    outcome = "complete"
   687	    if payload.expected_outcomes and outcome not in payload.expected_outcomes:
   688	        outcome = payload.expected_outcomes[0]
   689	    digest = hashlib.sha256(
   690	        f"{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:{payload.model}".encode("utf-8")
   691	    ).hexdigest()[:12]
   692	    return PhaseDispatchResult(
   693	        outcome=outcome,
   694	        handoff_id=f"dry-run:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:{digest}",
   695	        provider=payload.provider,
   696	        model_used=payload.model,
   697	        dispatch_tier="dry_run",
   698	        warnings=[],
   699	        agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   700	    )
   701	
   702	
   703	def _report_terminal_capacity(
   704	    result: PhaseDispatchResult,
   705	    reporter: Callable[[PhaseDispatchResult], Any],
   706	) -> None:
   707	    """Report a terminal capacity result without changing the dispatch outcome."""
   708	    error_class = getattr(result.error_class, "value", result.error_class)
   709	    if error_class not in {"capacity", "capacity_exhausted"}:
   710	        return
   711	    try:
   712	        reporter(result)
   713	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — reporting is best effort
   714	        logger.warning(
   715	            "Provider capacity reporting failed for agent_id=%s: %s",
   716	            result.agent_id,
   717	            exc,
   718	        )
   719	
   720	
   721	def dispatch_phase(
   722	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   723	    *,
   724	    runner: ProviderRunner | None = None,
   725	    dry_run: bool = False,
   726	    rate_limit_reporter: Callable[[PhaseDispatchResult], Any] = (
   727	        report_vendor_limit_result
   728	    ),
   729	) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   730	    """Dispatch a phase payload through a provider adapter.
   731	
   732	    Production harnesses can pass *runner* to invoke their provider-specific
   733	    execution surface. Without a runner, unsupported/nonconfigured adapters
   734	    return a structured fallback result so the SKILL.md layer can continue
   735	    through inline execution. Terminal capacity reporting is best effort and
   736	    never replaces the dispatch result.
   737	    """
   738	    if dry_run:
   739	        result = _dry_run_result(payload)
   740	    elif payload.provider not in _SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS:
   741	        result = _fallback_result(
   742	            payload, f"adapter unavailable for provider {payload.provider!r}"
   743	        )
   744	    elif runner is None:
   745	        if payload.provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER:
   746	            result = _dispatch_local(payload)
   747	        else:
   748	            result = _fallback_result(
   749	                payload,
   750	                f"adapter unavailable for provider {payload.provider!r} in this runtime",
   751	            )
   752	    else:
   753	        result = normalize_dispatch_result(runner(payload), payload, "harness")
   754	
   755	    _report_terminal_capacity(result, rate_limit_reporter)
   756	    return result

FILE:openspec/changes/make-the-orchestrator-obey-the-router/design.md
     1	# Design: Make the orchestrator obey the router
     2	
     3	## Decision D1 — Routing is injected at the host seam
     4	
     5	The roadmap state machine accepts a routing resolver protocol and invokes it before
     6	every synchronous `execute_roadmap` host dispatch. The resolver is responsible for bridge/coordinator access; the
     7	state machine never imports a vendor SDK or executes a model directly. Legacy callers
     8	may omit the resolver during migration, but a configured resolver fails closed when it
     9	is unavailable, raises, or returns malformed data.
    10	
    11	## Decision D2 — Dispatch context is immutable and versioned
    12	
    13	Every routed attempt carries schema version 1, the router's durable `decision_id`, the
    14	roadmap item and phase, an attempt number, a dispatch/ledger work ID, and the complete
    15	selected assignment. Canonical isolation is copied to the host envelope as one of
    16	`none`, `worktree`, or `sandbox`. The state machine validates and deep-copies this
    17	context so host code cannot mutate the router's decision in place.
    18	
    19	## Decision D3 — Completion must prove the active routed attempt
    20	
    21	A routed host result is terminal only when its proof echoes the durable active decision
    22	ID, dispatch work ID, observed agent ID, and expected ledger status. Completed work
    23	advances the phase. Capacity failures first persist the policy decision: WAIT preserves
    24	the lane and pause window, while SWITCH excludes the observed lane and requests a fresh
    25	router decision. Failed work closes the attempt and fails the item. Vendor-limit
    26	status, policy action, and any WAIT pause window are committed in one checkpoint save;
    27	a configured cost ceiling without authoritative routed cost evidence fails closed.
    28	The host-owned
    29	resolver/reconciler boundary supplies coordinator ledger evidence; the state machine
    30	validates that evidence against its checkpoint and never treats host mutation of the
    31	dispatch copy as authority. Retrying the same decision or accepting a stale,
    32	mismatched, unavailable, or unknown result fails closed.
    33	
    34	## Decision D4 — Loop safety is durable state
    35	
    36	The checkpoint records a global iteration count, a durable-progress fingerprint,
    37	consecutive no-progress count, and the most recent escalation. A durable item, phase,
    38	or ledger transition changes the fingerprint and resets the no-progress count. Hitting
    39	either configured cap checkpoints the escalation before execution parks, so restart
    40	cannot erase the guard or duplicate the escalation. Resumption requires an explicit
    41	host acknowledgement; prepared work is reconciled before any new submission, and a
    42	counter-based escalation parks again unless the host intentionally raises the relevant
    43	positive cap.
    44	
    45	## Decision D5 — Additive migration preserves current callers
    46	
    47	The opt-in delegated batch lifecycle is outside this change: it prepares requests and
    48	applies collected results through a distinct durable contract rather than invoking the
    49	synchronous phase `dispatch_fn` seam. Routing that lifecycle requires a separate change.
    50	
    51	The routing resolver and safety state are additive. Existing checkpoints deserialize
    52	with empty safety state, and callers without a resolver retain the current host-assisted
    53	path until the skill host wires the bridge. The new global iteration and no-progress
    54	guards intentionally bound both legacy and routed execution; legacy policies configured
    55	above the no-progress cap may park at the safety boundary first. Once a resolver is supplied, no implicit
    56	static route or unverified success is accepted.
FILE:openspec/changes/make-the-orchestrator-obey-the-router/specs/roadmap-orchestration/spec.md
     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Executed Routing Decisions
     4	
     5	`autopilot-roadmap` SHALL obtain and durably persist a validated routing decision before each synchronous `execute_roadmap` host dispatch. The immutable dispatch context SHALL include a decision identifier, selected agent/vendor/model/location, canonical dg-05 isolation, dispatch mode, and ledger work/attempt correlation. The host seam SHALL preserve this context unchanged; the state machine SHALL not call a model SDK or select a vendor locally.
     6	
     7	#### Scenario: Ledger-verified vendor switch
     8	
     9	WHEN a submitted attempt reports a vendor-limit result
    10	AND active roadmap policy authorizes switching lanes
    11	THEN the orchestrator SHALL resolve a fresh alternate assignment excluding the observed limited lane
    12	AND persist a new attempt before redispatching the same item and phase
    13	AND accept success only when the terminal VendorResultEnvelope/ledger completion matches that attempt's decision identifier and observed lane
    14	AND reject a stale, mismatched, or unavailable completion without treating the phase as complete.
    15	
    16	#### Scenario: Routed vendor limit honors wait policy
    17	
    18	WHEN a routed attempt reports a vendor-limit result
    19	AND active roadmap policy requires waiting
    20	THEN the orchestrator SHALL close the attempt as vendor-limited and persist `policy_action: wait`
    21	AND SHALL persist the vendor pause and reset window without resolving or dispatching an alternate lane.
    22	
    23	#### Scenario: Router unavailable
    24	
    25	WHEN no validated routing decision can be obtained from the configured resolver
    26	THEN the orchestrator SHALL use only a declared static fallback assignment with canonical isolation
    27	OR SHALL checkpoint a fail-closed escalation
    28	AND SHALL NOT dispatch with an un-routed context.
    29	
    30	### Requirement: Roadmap Loop Safety Caps
    31	
    32	The roadmap execution loop SHALL enforce durable global iteration and no-progress safeguards. Their counters and last durable-progress fingerprint SHALL be checkpointed before each dispatch and survive a resumed process.
    33	
    34	#### Scenario: Stuck dispatch trips the cap
    35	
    36	WHEN the configured iteration cap is reached or consecutive iterations produce no durable item, phase, or correlated-ledger transition
    37	THEN the loop SHALL checkpoint an explicit parked/escalated outcome and return it without continuing to dispatch.
    38	
    39	#### Scenario: Resume does not duplicate a submitted attempt
    40	
    41	WHEN a process stops after persisting a prepared attempt and before terminal completion
    42	THEN a resumed process SHALL reconcile the correlated ledger state before any new submission
    43	AND SHALL NOT issue a duplicate dispatch for that attempt.

    59	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is_domain_allowed(
    60	    p_agent_id TEXT,
    61	    p_domain TEXT
    62	)
    63	RETURNS JSONB
    64	LANGUAGE plpgsql
    65	AS $$
    66	DECLARE
    67	    v_profile_id UUID;
    68	    v_policy RECORD;
    69	    v_allowed BOOLEAN := false;
    70	    v_reason TEXT := 'no_matching_policy';
    71	    v_policy_id UUID;
    72	BEGIN
    73	    -- Get agent's profile ID
    74	    SELECT pa.profile_id INTO v_profile_id
    75	    FROM agent_profile_assignments pa
    76	    WHERE pa.agent_id = p_agent_id;
    77	
    78	    -- Check policies: profile-specific first, then global (NULL profile_id)
    79	    -- Higher priority (lower number) wins
    80	    FOR v_policy IN
    81	        SELECT np.*
    82	        FROM network_policies np
    83	        WHERE np.enabled = true
    84	          AND (np.profile_id = v_profile_id OR np.profile_id IS NULL)
    85	          AND (
    86	              p_domain = np.domain_pattern
    87	              OR p_domain LIKE REPLACE(np.domain_pattern, '*', '%')
    88	          )
    89	        ORDER BY
    90	            CASE WHEN np.profile_id IS NOT NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,  -- profile-specific first
    91	            np.priority ASC
    92	        LIMIT 1
    93	    LOOP
    94	        v_allowed := (v_policy.action = 'allow');
    95	        v_reason := v_policy.action;
    96	        v_policy_id := v_policy.id;
    97	    END LOOP;
    98	
    99	    -- Log the access attempt
   100	    INSERT INTO network_access_log (agent_id, domain, allowed, policy_id, reason)
   101	    VALUES (p_agent_id, p_domain, v_allowed, v_policy_id, v_reason);
   102	
   103	    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
   104	        'allowed', v_allowed,
   105	        'domain', p_domain,
   106	        'reason', v_reason,
   107	        'policy_id', v_policy_id
   108	    );
   109	END;
   110	$$;

   371	    async def check_network_access(
   372	        self,
   373	        agent_id: str,
   374	        domain: str,
   375	    ) -> PolicyDecision:
   376	        """Check network access using native NetworkPolicyService.
   377	
   378	        The service is built over *this engine's* database client. It used to
   379	        call ``get_network_policy_service()``, a process-global that resolves
   380	        its own client via ``get_db()`` — so an engine constructed with an
   381	        explicit client silently made its network decisions against a
   382	        different database. When the two disagree the RPC raises and
   383	        ``check_domain`` falls back to the default policy, which denies; a
   384	        wrong-database read therefore surfaced as ordinary denials rather than
   385	        as an error, and stayed invisible. Flipping the ``DB_BACKEND`` default
   386	        is what finally exposed it.
   387	        """
   388	        from .network_policies import NetworkPolicyService, get_network_policy_service
   389	
   390	        service = (
   391	            NetworkPolicyService(self._db)
   392	            if self._db is not None
   393	            else get_network_policy_service()
   394	        )
   395	        try:
   396	            decision = await service.check_domain(
   397	                domain=domain, agent_id=agent_id
   398	            )
   399	            if decision.allowed:
   400	                return PolicyDecision.allow(
   401	                    reason=decision.reason or "network_permitted"
   402	                )
   403	            return PolicyDecision.deny(
   404	                reason=decision.reason or "network_denied"
   405	            )
   406	        except Exception as e:
   407	            return PolicyDecision.deny(f"network_error: {e}")
   408
