   356	def _combine_layers(layers: list[EnvironmentProfile]) -> EnvironmentProfile:
   357	    """Resolve each dimension from its first definitive layer."""
   358	    values = {"filesystem": False, "network": False}
   359	    dimension_sources: dict[str, str] = {}
   360	    layer_sources: dict[str, Source] = {}
   361	    details: dict[str, Any] = {}
   362	
   363	    for layer in layers:
   364	        reported = layer.details.get("dimension_sources", {})
   365	        if not isinstance(reported, dict):
   366	            continue
   367	        selected = False
   368	        for dimension in ("filesystem", "network"):
   369	            if dimension in dimension_sources or dimension not in reported:
   370	                continue
   371	            values[dimension] = getattr(layer.posture, dimension)
   372	            dimension_sources[dimension] = str(reported[dimension])
   373	            layer_sources[dimension] = layer.source
   374	            selected = True
   375	        if selected:
   376	            for key, value in layer.details.items():
   377	                if key != "dimension_sources":
   378	                    details.setdefault(key, value)
   379	
   380	    for dimension in ("filesystem", "network"):
   381	        if dimension not in dimension_sources:
   382	            dimension_sources[dimension] = "default"
   383	            layer_sources[dimension] = "default"
   384	    details["dimension_sources"] = dimension_sources
   385	
   386	    source = layer_sources["filesystem"]
   387	    if source == "default":
   388	        source = layer_sources["network"]
   389	    return EnvironmentProfile(
   390	        posture=IsolationPosture(
   391	            filesystem=values["filesystem"],
   392	            network=values["network"],
   393	        ),
   394	        source=source,
   395	        details=details,
   396	    )

     1	# Design: Isolation posture detection
     2	
     3	## Context
     4	
     5	The detector collapses filesystem workspace isolation and network restriction into one
     6	boolean. dg-07 needs those facts independently while current callers depend on
     7	`isolation_provided`.
     8	
     9	## Decisions
    10	
    11	### D1 — Nested factual booleans
    12	
    13	`IsolationPosture.filesystem` means the harness supplies a per-session workspace.
    14	`IsolationPosture.network` means it enforces restricted egress. Neither claims a
    15	containment strength.
    16	
    17	### D2 — Read and construction compatibility
    18	
    19	`EnvironmentProfile.isolation_provided` derives from `posture.filesystem`. The legacy
    20	constructor maps its boolean to filesystem and defaults network false. Supplying both
    21	forms is an error.
    22	
    23	### D3 — Signals prove only their own dimension
    24	
    25	Precedence is applied independently per dimension across explicit env, coordinator,
    26	heuristic, and default layers. Exact Claude/Codex cloud markers prove filesystem;
    27	`CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED` proves network. A higher filesystem result does not
    28	prevent a lower layer from resolving network, while a structured coordinator network
    29	value blocks a lower network heuristic. The canonical coordinator field is
    30	`isolation_posture`; malformed canonical data rejects that layer and never falls back
    31	to a simultaneously supplied legacy boolean.
    32	
    33	### D4 — Migrate only worktree decision points
    34	
    35	Worktree and merge entrypoints read `posture.filesystem`; other callers retain the
    36	compatibility property. Fallback imports expose the same surface and output is unchanged.
    37	
    38	## Failure and verification
    39	
    40	Unknown explicit values fall through. Malformed coordinator values do not coerce.
    41	Tests first pin the model and truth table, then subprocess behavior. Focused/full tests,
    42	Ruff, strict OpenSpec validation, and multi-vendor review gate landing.

     1	## MODIFIED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Detection SHALL follow a documented precedence order
     4	
     5	`EnvironmentProfile.detect()` SHALL resolve filesystem and network independently in
     6	this precedence order, using the first definitive value for each dimension:
     7	
     8	1. Explicit env: `AGENT_EXECUTION_ENV=cloud|local` and legacy
     9	   `CLAUDE_CODE_CLOUD=1` resolve filesystem only.
    10	2. Coordinator: canonical `isolation_posture` boolean members resolve both dimensions;
    11	   legacy boolean `isolation_provided` resolves filesystem only.
    12	3. Heuristic: `/.dockerenv`, non-empty `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`,
    13	   `CODESPACES=true`, `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`, or the exact pair
    14	   `CODEX_CI=1` plus `CODEX_PERMISSION_PROFILE=:workspace` resolve filesystem.
    15	   `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1` resolves network independently.
    16	4. Default: every unresolved dimension is not provided.
    17	
    18	The compatibility `source` SHALL identify the filesystem layer, or the network layer
    19	when filesystem reaches default and network does not.
    20	
    21	#### Scenario: Explicit filesystem and coordinator network compose
    22	
    23	WHEN `AGENT_EXECUTION_ENV=local` is set
    24	AND the coordinator reports `isolation_posture={filesystem: true, network: true}`
    25	THEN filesystem isolation SHALL be not provided with explicit-env provenance
    26	AND network isolation SHALL be provided with coordinator provenance.
    27	
    28	#### Scenario: Coordinator network decision outranks heuristic
    29	
    30	WHEN the coordinator reports a structured network value of false
    31	AND `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1`
    32	THEN network isolation SHALL remain not provided with coordinator provenance.
    33	
    34	#### Scenario: Network-only heuristic has a non-default source
    35	
    36	WHEN no filesystem signal matches
    37	AND `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED=1`
    38	THEN filesystem isolation SHALL be not provided
    39	AND network isolation SHALL be provided
    40	AND the compatibility source SHALL be `heuristic`.
    41	
    42	#### Scenario: No signal preserves local defaults
    43	
    44	WHEN no explicit, coordinator, or heuristic signal resolves either dimension
    45	THEN both dimensions SHALL be not provided
    46	AND the compatibility source SHALL be `default`.
    47	
    48	#### Scenario: Explicit filesystem value outranks coordinator and heuristic
    49	
    50	WHEN `AGENT_EXECUTION_ENV=local`
    51	AND the coordinator reports filesystem isolation
    52	AND a filesystem heuristic also matches
    53	THEN filesystem isolation SHALL be not provided with explicit-env provenance.
    54	
    55	#### Scenario: Coordinator filesystem value outranks heuristic
    56	
    57	WHEN no explicit filesystem value is set
    58	AND the coordinator reports filesystem isolation as not provided
    59	AND a filesystem heuristic matches
    60	THEN filesystem isolation SHALL remain not provided with coordinator provenance.
    61	
    62	#### Scenario: Filesystem heuristic fires when higher layers are silent
    63	
    64	WHEN explicit configuration and the coordinator do not resolve filesystem
    65	AND a filesystem heuristic matches
    66	THEN filesystem isolation SHALL be provided with heuristic provenance
    67	AND `WORKTREE_DEBUG=1` SHALL emit the matched heuristic in the profile dump.
    68	
    69	## ADDED Requirements
    70	
    71	### Requirement: Isolation posture reports filesystem and network as independent dimensions
    72	
    73	`EnvironmentProfile.detect()` SHALL return an isolation posture that reports filesystem isolation and network isolation as two independently-valued dimensions, so that a caller can act on one without asserting anything about the other.
    74	
    75	A container provides strong filesystem isolation and entirely unrestricted egress. A single boolean cannot express that pairing, and every downstream consumer that needs to say "skip the filesystem sandbox here, still apply the network allowlist" is forced to guess.
    76	
    77	#### Scenario: Container posture distinguishes the two dimensions
    78	
    79	WHEN `EnvironmentProfile.detect()` runs inside a container that isolates the filesystem but applies no egress restriction
    80	THEN the returned posture SHALL report filesystem isolation as provided
    81	AND SHALL report network isolation as not provided.
    82	
    83	#### Scenario: Dimensions are separately addressable
    84	
    85	WHEN a caller inspects the returned posture
    86	THEN the filesystem dimension SHALL be readable without consulting the network dimension
    87	AND the network dimension SHALL be readable without consulting the filesystem dimension.
    88	
    89	### Requirement: The `isolation_provided` boolean remains a supported compatibility surface
    90	
    91	`EnvironmentProfile` SHALL continue to expose `isolation_provided` as a boolean-valued compatibility property whose value is the filesystem-isolation dimension, so that existing callers observe no behavior change.
    92	
    93	The precedence ladder and short-circuit semantics already specified for `isolation_provided` continue to apply unchanged when read through this property.
    94	
    95	#### Scenario: Existing boolean caller is unaffected
    96	
    97	WHEN existing code reads `EnvironmentProfile.detect().isolation_provided`
    98	THEN the value SHALL equal the filesystem-isolation dimension of the posture
    99	AND no call site SHALL require modification to keep its current behavior.
   100	
   101	#### Scenario: Worktree entrypoints read the filesystem dimension
   102	
   103	WHEN `worktree.py` or `merge_worktrees.py` decides whether to short-circuit a git worktree mutation
   104	THEN the decision SHALL be taken from the filesystem-isolation dimension
   105	AND the observable short-circuit behavior SHALL be identical to the behavior specified for `isolation_provided`.
   106	
   107	### Requirement: Detection SHALL identify cloud harnesses that expose no container heuristic
   108	
   109	The container-heuristic stage of the detection ladder SHALL recognize cloud harness environments that expose none of `/.dockerenv`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, or `CODESPACES`, and SHALL report filesystem isolation as provided in those environments.
   110	
   111	This closes a demonstrated gap: a cloud harness exposing none of the three existing signals returned `isolation_provided=false, source="default"`, so `worktree.py setup` attempted a real worktree and failed against the already-checked-out branch.
   112	
   113	#### Scenario: Cloud harness without the legacy signals is detected
   114	
   115	WHEN `EnvironmentProfile.detect()` runs in a cloud harness that exposes none of `/.dockerenv`, `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST`, or `CODESPACES`
   116	AND no explicit `AGENT_EXECUTION_ENV` value is set
   117	AND the coordinator reports nothing for the agent-id
   118	THEN detection SHALL report filesystem isolation as provided
   119	AND SHALL report a source other than `default`.
   120	
   121	#### Scenario: Worktree setup no longer fails on the checked-out branch
   122	
   123	WHEN `worktree.py setup` runs in that same cloud harness
   124	THEN it SHALL short-circuit the worktree creation
   125	AND SHALL NOT attempt a git worktree against the already-checked-out branch.
   126	
   127	#### Scenario: Explicit configuration still outranks the heuristic
   128	
   129	WHEN `AGENT_EXECUTION_ENV` is set explicitly
   130	OR the coordinator reports a value for the agent-id
   131	THEN that value SHALL take precedence for each dimension it reports
   132	AND an independent network-only signal MAY still report network isolation when an
   133	explicit or coordinator value resolves only the filesystem dimension
   134	AND the documented precedence order SHALL be preserved.
   135	
   136	#### Scenario: Coordinator payload is typed and backward compatible
   137	
   138	WHEN the coordinator returns `isolation_posture` with boolean `filesystem` and
   139	`network` members
   140	THEN both dimensions SHALL be used with coordinator provenance
   141	AND when it instead returns the legacy boolean `isolation_provided`, that value SHALL
   142	map to filesystem while network remains not provided
   143	AND malformed or non-boolean values SHALL fall through rather than use truthiness
   144	coercion.

FILE:openspec/changes/pin-isolation-contract/design.md
     1	# Design: Pin the isolation contract between router and dispatch
     2	
     3	## Decision D1 — One pure module serves both runtime paths
     4	
     5	`agent-coordinator/src/isolation_contract.py` is the one definition of
     6	`none`, `worktree`, and `sandbox`. It is stdlib-only and exports the static
     7	type, allowed values, `IsolationContractError`, validation, an
     8	`IsolationResolution(value, source)` result, and a pure per-mode helper.
     9	
    10	The coordinator imports it normally. The coordinator-unreachable fallback
    11	loads the same file through its checkout-root import shim. Published dg-04
    12	schemas retain serialized enums, but parity tests derive expected values from
    13	D1 rather than hand-maintained runtime definitions.
    14	
    15	## Decision D2 — Resolution records absence, invalid values, and provenance
    16	
    17	The ladder is: a reachable router's present valid value (`source=router`); the
    18	matching configured agent's mode override then entry default
    19	(`source=agents_yaml`); and `none` (`source=default`). Absent values fall
    20	through. A present invalid value raises `IsolationContractError` naming the
    21	rung; empty values are never silently coerced with `or "none"`.
    22	
    23	`get_agent_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode=None, *, agent_id=None)` stays
    24	source-compatible. Router and fallback call sites that know identity supply it,
    25	preventing local/remote entries of the same type from depending on YAML order.
    26	
    27	## Decision D3 — Mode overrides apply before assignments are emitted
    28	
    29	`ModeConfig` gains optional `isolation`. `vendor_registry` exposes mode-aware
    30	information and the resolver computes assignment isolation after dispatch mode
    31	is known. The fallback uses the same helper before filtering or sorting a lane.
    32	Dispatch-config projection and the skills review dispatcher parse the additive
    33	field. dg-06 execution wiring and dg-07 enforcement remain excluded.
    34	
    35	## Decision D4 — Widening requires an explicit amendment
    36	
    37	`container` is not valid in this change. Before
    38	`add-sandboxed-harness-execution` can introduce that posture, a future OpenSpec
    39	amendment must update the canonical type and values, both published schema
    40	enums, validation and precedence tests, and the router/fallback parity matrix.
    41	Until that amendment lands, every producer and consumer rejects `container`
    42	as an invalid present value rather than treating it as absence or `none`.

     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: The isolation vocabulary SHALL be specified once and referenced by both producer and consumer
     4	
     5	The isolation vocabulary — `none`, `worktree`, and `sandbox` — SHALL be defined in exactly one location, and both the task router that emits an isolation value and the dispatch layer that consumes it SHALL reference that definition rather than restating the value set.
     6	
     7	The router already emits an isolation value and the dispatch layer already consumes one, but no artifact defines what the values mean. Two independent restatements of a vocabulary drift silently, and the first divergence is a dispatch that runs under a posture nobody intended.
     8	
     9	#### Scenario: Producer and consumer share one definition
    10	
    11	WHEN the task router emits an isolation value
    12	AND the dispatch layer resolves that value
    13	THEN both SHALL derive the accepted value set from the same definition
    14	AND neither SHALL hard-code an independent copy of the vocabulary.
    15	
    16	#### Scenario: Static contracts remain in parity with the canonical vocabulary
    17	
    18	WHEN the published routing OpenAPI or routing-policy schema is checked
    19	THEN its isolation enum SHALL equal the canonical vocabulary
    20	AND the check SHALL fail if either contract drifts from the runtime definition.
    21	
    22	#### Scenario: An unrecognized isolation value is rejected
    23	
    24	WHEN a value outside the defined vocabulary reaches the dispatch layer
    25	THEN resolution SHALL fail with an explicit error naming the offending value
    26	AND dispatch SHALL NOT proceed under a silently substituted posture.
    27	
    28	### Requirement: Isolation resolution SHALL follow a documented precedence ladder
    29	
    30	Effective isolation SHALL be resolved by a documented precedence ladder: the task router when it is reachable, then `get_agent_isolation()` reading `agents.yaml`, then `none`.
    31	
    32	This mirrors the precedence structure already established for execution-environment detection, so that one mental model covers both.
    33	
    34	#### Scenario: Router value wins when the router is reachable
    35	
    36	WHEN the task router is reachable
    37	AND it returns an isolation value for the dispatch
    38	THEN that value SHALL be the effective isolation
    39	AND `agents.yaml` SHALL NOT override it.
    40	
    41	#### Scenario: agents.yaml supplies the value when the router is silent
    42	
    43	WHEN the task router is reachable but returns no isolation value for the dispatch
    44	THEN `get_agent_isolation()` SHALL supply the effective isolation from `agents.yaml`.
    45	
    46	#### Scenario: Coordinator-unreachable yields a decision, not an error
    47	
    48	WHEN the coordinator is unreachable
    49	THEN resolution SHALL yield a defined isolation decision rather than raising
    50	AND the decision SHALL fall through to `agents.yaml`, then to `none`
    51	AND the resolved decision SHALL record which rung of the ladder produced it.
    52	
    53	#### Scenario: Absence falls through
    54	
    55	WHEN a reachable router supplies no isolation value
    56	OR a configured agent has no matching per-mode override
    57	THEN resolution SHALL fall through to the next rung and record that source.
    58	
    59	#### Scenario: Invalid presence fails closed
    60	
    61	WHEN any supplied isolation value is outside the canonical vocabulary
    62	THEN resolution SHALL raise an explicit contract error naming the source rung
    63	AND SHALL NOT treat that invalid value as an absent value.
    64	
    65	
    66	### Requirement: Isolation SHALL resolve for an (agent_type, dispatch_mode) pair
    67	
    68	Effective isolation SHALL resolve for an `(agent_type, dispatch_mode)` pair rather than for an agent type alone, and `agents.yaml` SHALL be able to express a per-mode override within a single agent entry.
    69	
    70	`agents.yaml` already implies per-mode postures — a `review` mode carrying read-only flags beside an `alternative` mode carrying write flags — and today cannot express the difference.
    71	
    72	#### Scenario: Review and alternative modes resolve differently under one entry
    73	
    74	WHEN one agent entry declares a per-mode isolation override for `review`
    75	AND the same entry declares a different posture for `alternative`
    76	THEN resolving `(agent_type, "review")` SHALL return the review posture
    77	AND resolving `(agent_type, "alternative")` SHALL return the alternative posture.
    78	
    79	#### Scenario: Entry-level posture applies when no per-mode override exists
    80	
    81	WHEN an agent entry declares an isolation posture with no per-mode override
    82	THEN every dispatch mode for that entry SHALL resolve to the entry-level posture.
    83	
    84	#### Scenario: Exact agent identity disambiguates repeated agent types
    85	
    86	WHEN more than one `agents.yaml` entry has the same agent type
    87	AND the resolver is given the dispatched agent identity
    88	THEN its per-mode or entry-level posture SHALL be resolved from that exact entry
    89	AND SHALL NOT depend on YAML ordering.
    90	
    91	#### Scenario: Router and local fallback agree on a configured mode override
    92	
    93	WHEN an agent entry defines a per-mode isolation override
    94	AND both paths select that agent and mode
    95	THEN both paths SHALL emit the same effective isolation value.

   221	def _validated_routing_decision(value: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   222	    """Return a detached routing decision with a canonical dg-05 assignment."""
   223	    decision = copy.deepcopy(dict(value))
   224	    decision_id = decision.get("decision_id")
   225	    assignment = decision.get("assignment")
   226	    if not isinstance(decision_id, str) or not decision_id:
   227	        raise ValueError("routing decision_id must be a non-empty string")
   228	    if not isinstance(assignment, Mapping):
   229	        raise ValueError("routing assignment must be an object")
   230	    required = {"agent_id", "vendor_type", "location", "isolation", "dispatch_mode", "model", "endpoint_kind"}
   231	    if not required.issubset(assignment):
   232	        raise ValueError("routing assignment is missing required fields")
   233	    if any(
   234	        not isinstance(assignment[field], str) or not assignment[field]
   235	        for field in required
   236	    ):
   237	        raise ValueError("routing assignment fields must be non-empty strings")

   178	
   179	### Capability: OS-level isolation enforcement at dispatch
   180	
   181	A `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` renderer turns a resolved isolation decision plus the
   182	coordinator's network policy and worktree root into a runtime-specific policy document and an
   183	argv wrapper. `CliVendorAdapter` applies the wrapper between `build_command()` and
   184	`subprocess.run()` — one injection site covering every current and future vendor CLI.
   185	
   186	The initial runtime target is `srt` (Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap plus seccomp on Linux), the
   187	same mechanism behind Claude Code's own `/sandbox`. The renderer sits behind a `render_*` seam
   188	so a container or OpenShell backend is an addition rather than a rewrite — a requirement, not
   189	speculative generality, given that both candidate runtimes are explicitly pre-1.0.
   190	
   191	**Acceptance Outcomes:**
   192	- `isolation: sandbox` produces observable filesystem and network restriction on a dispatched vendor CLI
   193	- The coordinator's existing network policy is enforced at the socket without policy being re-authored anywhere
   194	- Missing runtime or unsupported platform degrades to unsandboxed dispatch with a warning and an audit event
   195	- Adding a second runtime backend requires only a new renderer function
   196	
   197	### Capability: Egress gateway and request-time secret boundary
   198	
   252	- **Enforcement must not re-author policy.** Network policy is authored once, in the
   253	  coordinator. Runtime policy documents are *renderings* of it. A second source of truth for
   254	  allowed domains is a failure of this epic.
   255	- **One resolver, one cost table.** The merged `model_routing` resolver and catalog are extended,
   256	  never paralleled. A second scoring path or a second vendor cost store is a failure of this epic
   257	  on the same grounds as a second policy source.
   258	- **Degradation must be loud, never silent.** `srt` requires macOS or Linux with bubblewrap,
   259	  socat, and ripgrep. Where unavailable, dispatch proceeds unsandboxed with a warning and an
   260	  audit event, following the pattern already established in `vendor_health.py`. Failing closed
   261	  would break every developer on an unsupported platform for a control that its own authors
   262	  describe as a defense against confused agents rather than determined ones.
   263	- **The threat model is bounded and must be stated as such.** `srt`'s documentation is explicit
   264	  that an allowlist containing `github.com` is an exfiltration channel, that domain fronting
   265	  works, and that an exposed Docker socket is a full escape. This repository's workflow requires
   266	  `github.com`. Specs must claim protection against accidental credential reads and unplanned
   267	  egress — not containment of a determined adversary.
   268	- **One execution surface per change-id.** Items re-homed from `repo-improvement` must not be
   269	  tracked as active in two roadmaps simultaneously.
   270	- **Ordering resolves the conflict.** The structured vendor result channel and the dispatch
   271	  wrapper modify the same `CliVendorAdapter` methods and must not run concurrently.
   272	- **Existing callers keep working.** Widening `isolation_provided` to a posture must not break
   273	  `worktree.py` or `merge_worktrees.py`.
   274	- **A bypassable gateway is worse than no gateway.** The egress gateway deploys only where the
   275	  dg-03 posture proves the workload cannot route around it. DNS-only interception on the local
   276	  uid, or a second MITM inside the managed cloud harness, are explicitly rejected deployments:
   277	  each would report containment that does not exist, which is the silent-degradation failure
   278	  mode this epic forbids.

     1	"""Vendor health check: verify all configured vendors' readiness.
     2	
     3	Design Decisions:
     4	  D5: Dual-use — standalone CLI script + importable module for WatchdogService.
     5	  D6: No inference probes — uses can_dispatch() + API key resolution only.
     6	  D7: Watchdog events on coordinator_agent channel.
     7	"""
     8	
     9	from __future__ import annotations
    10	
    11	import argparse
    12	import json
    13	import os
    14	import shutil
    15	import sys
    16	from urllib.error import URLError
    17	from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
    18	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
    19	from pathlib import Path
    20	
    21	
    22	@dataclass
    23	class VendorHealth:
    24	    """Health status for a single vendor agent."""
    25	
    26	    agent_id: str
    27	    vendor_type: str
    28	    cli_command: str
    29	    cli_installed: bool = False
    30	    api_key_available: bool = False
    31	    dispatch_modes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    32	    models: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    33	    healthy: bool = False
    34	    error: str | None = None
    35	
    36	
    37	@dataclass
    38	class HealthReport:
    39	    """Aggregate health report for all vendors."""
    40	
    41	    vendors: list[VendorHealth] = field(default_factory=list)
    42	    healthy_count: int = 0
    43	    total_count: int = 0
    44	
    45	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    46	        return {
    47	            "vendors": [asdict(v) for v in self.vendors],
    48	            "healthy_count": self.healthy_count,
    49	            "total_count": self.total_count,
    50	        }
    51	
    52	
    53	def check_vendor(agent_id: str, agent_config: dict) -> VendorHealth:
    54	    """Check health of a single vendor from its agents.yaml config."""
    55	    cli = agent_config.get("cli", {})
    56	    command = cli.get("command", "")
    57	    vendor_type = agent_config.get("type", "unknown")
    58	
    59	    health = VendorHealth(
    60	        agent_id=agent_id,
    61	        vendor_type=vendor_type,
    62	        cli_command=command,
    63	    )
    64	
    65	    # Check 1: CLI installed
    66	    if command:
    67	        health.cli_installed = shutil.which(command) is not None
    68	
    69	    # Check 2: Available dispatch modes
    70	    dispatch_modes = cli.get("dispatch_modes", {})
    71	    for mode_name, mode_config in dispatch_modes.items():
    72	        if health.cli_installed:
    73	            health.dispatch_modes.append(mode_name)
    74	
    75	    # Check 3: Models configured
    76	    model = cli.get("model")
    77	    if model:
    78	        health.models.append(model)
    79	    health.models.extend(cli.get("model_fallbacks", []))
    80	
    81	    # Check 4: API key availability (CLI-declared env var, SDK section, or
    82	    # direct api_key). cli.api_key_env is a credential the CLI itself needs
    83	    # to serve a request (pi: OPENROUTER_API_KEY, issue #383).
    84	    sdk = agent_config.get("sdk") or {}
    85	    cli_api_key_env = cli.get("api_key_env")
    86	    api_key_env = cli_api_key_env or sdk.get("api_key_env")
    87	    if api_key_env:
    88	        health.api_key_available = bool(os.environ.get(api_key_env))
    89	    else:
    90	        # Check if api_key is configured directly
    91	        api_key = agent_config.get("api_key")
    92	        if api_key and not api_key.startswith("${"):
    93	            health.api_key_available = True
    94	        elif api_key and api_key.startswith("${"):
    95	            # Environment variable reference
    96	            env_var = api_key.strip("${}")
    97	            health.api_key_available = bool(os.environ.get(env_var))
    98	
    99	    # Determine overall health. When the CLI declares a required credential,
   100	    # a present binary without it cannot serve requests — fail closed. D6
   101	    # still holds: this is env-var resolution, not an inference probe.
   102	    if cli_api_key_env:
   103	        health.healthy = health.cli_installed and health.api_key_available
   104	    else:
   105	        health.healthy = health.cli_installed or health.api_key_available
   106	
   107	    has_probe_method = bool(command or api_key_env or agent_config.get("api_key"))
   108	    if not has_probe_method:
   109	        health.error = "no_probe_method"
   110	
   111	    return health
   112	
   113	
   114	def load_agents_yaml(path: Path | None = None) -> dict:
   115	    """Load explicit config, then public HTTP config, then a local fallback."""
   116	    import yaml
   117	
   118	    explicit = path or (
   119	        Path(os.environ["AGENTS_YAML"]).expanduser()
   120	        if os.environ.get("AGENTS_YAML")
   121	        else None
   122	    )
   123	    if explicit and explicit.exists():
   124	        with open(explicit) as f:
   125	            return yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
   126	
   127	    base_url = os.environ.get("COORDINATION_API_URL")
   128	    if base_url:
   129	        request = Request(
   130	            f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/agents/dispatch-configs",
   131	            headers={"User-Agent": "agentic-coding-tools/0.1"},
   132	        )
   133	        try:
   134	            with urlopen(request, timeout=3.0) as response:
   135	                payload = json.loads(response.read())
   136	            if isinstance(payload, dict):
   137	                agents = payload.get("agents", [])
   138	                if isinstance(agents, list):
   139	                    return {
   140	                        "agents": {
   141	                            item["agent_id"]: item
   142	                            for item in agents
   143	                            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("agent_id")
   144	                        }
   145	                    }
   146	                return payload
   147	        except (URLError, OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError):
   148	            pass
   149	
   150	    # Optional source-repository compatibility fallback.
   151	    candidates = [
   152	        Path.cwd() / "agent-coordinator" / "agents.yaml",
   153	    ]
   154	    for candidate in candidates:
   155	        if candidate.exists():
   156	            with open(candidate) as f:
   157	                return yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
   158	
   159	    return {}
   160	
   161	
   162	def check_all_vendors(agents_yaml_path: Path | None = None) -> HealthReport:
   163	    """Check health of all vendors configured in agents.yaml."""
   164	    config = load_agents_yaml(agents_yaml_path)
   165	    agents = config.get("agents", {})
   166	
   167	    report = HealthReport()
   168	    for agent_id, agent_config in agents.items():
   169	        health = check_vendor(agent_id, agent_config)
   170	        report.vendors.append(health)
   171	
   172	    report.total_count = len(report.vendors)
   173	    report.healthy_count = sum(1 for v in report.vendors if v.healthy)
   174	    return report
   175	
   176	
   177	def format_table(report: HealthReport) -> str:
   178	    """Format health report as a human-readable table."""
   179	    lines = []
   180	    header = f"{'Vendor':<18} {'CLI':<6} {'API Key':<9} {'Modes':<30} {'Models'}"
   181	    lines.append(header)
   182	    lines.append("-" * len(header))
   183	
   184	    for v in report.vendors:
   185	        cli_mark = "ok" if v.cli_installed else "-"
   186	        key_mark = "ok" if v.api_key_available else "-"
   187	        modes = ", ".join(v.dispatch_modes) if v.dispatch_modes else "-"
   188	        models = ", ".join(v.models) if v.models else "-"
   189	        lines.append(f"{v.agent_id:<18} {cli_mark:<6} {key_mark:<9} {modes:<30} {models}")
   190	
   191	    lines.append("")
   192	    lines.append(f"Healthy: {report.healthy_count}/{report.total_count}")
   193	    return "\n".join(lines)
   194	
   195	
   196	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   197	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Check vendor health status.")
   198	    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Output as JSON")
   199	    parser.add_argument("--agents-yaml", type=Path, default=None, help="Path to agents.yaml")
   200	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   201	
   202	    report = check_all_vendors(args.agents_yaml)
   203	
   204	    if args.json:
   205	        print(json.dumps(report.to_dict(), indent=2))
   206	    else:
   207	        print(format_table(report))
   208	
   209	    return 0
   210	
   211	
   212	if __name__ == "__main__":
   213	    sys.exit(main())
